title: [Core] DetachedBufferedBody content and owner are internal, so third-party IResponseBodySource consumers lose the body and cannot release the pooled owner
body:
## Summary
IResponseBodySource.TryDetachBufferedBody is public, but the DetachedBufferedBody it returns exposes its sequence and owner only internally. A third-party handler that calls it cannot read the body and cannot return the pooled buffer, which leaks the owner or loses data.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/DetachedBufferedBody.cs:39`

## Problem
DetachedBufferedBody is a public struct with public constructors, but Sequence, DetachOwner and DisposeOwnedResources are internal (DetachedBufferedBody.cs:39-52). TryDetachBufferedBody is a member of the public IResponseBodySource (IResponseBodySource.cs:13). On success the source gives up the data: BufferedResponseBodySource clears itself and marks itself disposed (Internal/BufferedResponseBodySource.cs:44-49) and Http2ResponseBodySource transfers its owner (Runtime/Transport/Http2/Http2ResponseBodySource.cs:169). First-party wrappers read .Sequence through InternalsVisibleTo (Runtime/Observability/ObservedResponseBodySource.cs:67, Runtime/Unity/Mobile/CountingResponseBodySource.cs:53).

**Failure scenario.** A third-party IHttpHandler tries the buffered fast path: body.TryDetachBufferedBody(out var d) returns true, the source is now empty, and d exposes nothing: the response body is gone and the SegmentedBuffer owner is never returned to ByteArrayPool (the pool's ActiveCount drifts).

## Suggested fix
Make Sequence and a Dispose/DetachOwner public on DetachedBufferedBody, or remove TryDetachBufferedBody from the public interface (internal interface implemented by first-party sources).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Either DetachedBufferedBody exposes its Sequence and a documented Dispose/owner release publicly, or TryDetachBufferedBody is removed from the public interface and kept internal
- [ ] A third-party handler can detach a buffered body, read it and release the pooled owner exactly once (or the API is no longer reachable from outside first-party code)
- [ ] a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Core/ fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Core] HappyEyeballsOptions.Validate accepts connection attempt delays below the RFC 8305 minimum of 10 ms
body:
## Summary
Validate does not reject or clamp ConnectionAttemptDelay values below the minimum that RFC 8305 section 5 allows. A tiny delay makes the client open all address families nearly at once, defeating the staggering the RFC requires.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/HappyEyeballsOptions.cs:76`

## Problem
Validate only rejects negative delays (HappyEyeballsOptions.cs:76-84); zero is valid for FamilyStaggerDelay and AttemptSpacingDelay. The connector uses the values as given (HappyEyeballsConnector.cs:69, 334-358) with no lower clamp. RFC 8305 Section 5: a subsequent connection attempt MUST NOT be started within 10 milliseconds of the previous one (recommended minimum 100 ms).

**Failure scenario.** An application sets AttemptSpacingDelay = TimeSpan.Zero to 'connect faster': for a host with many A/AAAA records the client starts connection attempts back to back (up to MaxConcurrentAttempts at once, each replaced as soon as it fails), which is the SYN burst the RFC forbids.

## Spec reference
RFC 8305 Section 5

## Suggested fix
Reject or clamp delays below 10 ms in Validate (and say so in the property docs).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Validate rejects (or clamps) connection attempt delays below 10 ms and the property XML doc states the rule
- [ ] a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Core/ fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [HTTP/2] Http2Options.EnablePush defaults to true although the transport refuses every pushed stream
body:
## Summary
The default initial SETTINGS advertises SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH = 1 while the transport resets every push, so servers waste work pushing resources the client discards. The XML doc also still cites RFC 7540.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/Http2Options.cs:10`

## Problem
_enablePush = true (Http2Options.cs:10) and IsDefault treats true as the default (line 247). The connection advertises it in the initial SETTINGS (Http2Settings.cs:106, Http2Connection.cs:180). The transport has no push support: RejectPushPromiseAsync decodes the promised field block to keep HPACK in sync and answers RST_STREAM(REFUSED_STREAM) for every PUSH_PROMISE (Http2Connection.ReadLoop.cs:1158-1204; 'PUSH_PROMISE blocks are always discarded', line 526). With ENABLE_PUSH=0 the same frame is a connection error (lines 1163-1165). The journals record the default as a fact, not as a decision (implementation-journal/2026-11-h2-conformance.md:38).

**Failure scenario.** A server or CDN that still pushes sends PUSH_PROMISE plus pushed HEADERS/DATA for each page resource; the client pays the bytes (mobile data), HPACK-decodes every promised block and writes a RST_STREAM each time. A hostile server may legally send an unbounded stream of PUSH_PROMISE blocks on a connection, each costing a header decode and a frame write, because the client invited them.

## Spec reference
RFC 9113 Sections 6.5.2 and 8.4

## Suggested fix
Default EnablePush to false so the initial SETTINGS carries SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH = 0, and keep true only as an explicit opt-in until push is implemented (or remove the option). Update IsDefault and the XML doc (which still cites RFC 7540).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Http2Options.EnablePush defaults to false and the initial SETTINGS carries SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH = 0 (RFC 9113 section 6.5.2); IsDefault and the XML doc are updated to cite RFC 9113
- [ ] true remains only an explicit opt-in until push is implemented, or the option is removed
- [ ] a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Core/ fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `core-protocol-06` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/core.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: protocol-impl.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Http2Options.cs:10 defaults _enablePush to true and IsDefault treats true as default (247); it is advertised in the initial SETTINGS (Http2Settings.cs:106, Http2Connection.cs:180). Every PUSH_PROMISE is refused: RejectPushPromiseAsync decodes the promised block and sends RST_STREAM(REFUSED_STREAM) (Http2Connection.ReadLoop.cs:1158-1204). The phase plan asked for ENABLE_PUSH = 0 (Development~/docs/phases/phase3b/overview.md:87, step-3b.9:38/103); the journals record the true default as fact (2026-11-h2-conformance.md:38, 2026-10-h2-headers-in.md:14), with no rationale. Not an RFC violation (RFC 9113 Section 8.4 lets a client enable push and refuse each promise), so this is wasted bytes and work with a pushing server, not wrong behaviour; most servers no longer push. The 'unbounded PUSH_PROMISE' cost is bounded per frame by the header limits and is no worse than other frame floods. Low: flip the default.

title: [Core] IsDefault has different meanings in ConnectionPoolOptions, Http2Options and StreamingOptions, and Http2Options carries test-only overrides
body:
## Summary
ConnectionPoolOptions.IsDefault means never assigned, while Http2Options and StreamingOptions define it as equal to the defaults, with default literals duplicated in several places. Http2Options also exposes test-only overrides in its public surface.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/Http2Options.cs:245`

## Problem
ConnectionPoolOptions.IsDefault returns !_explicitlySet (ConnectionPoolOptions.cs:232-235, #184). Http2Options.IsDefault compares each field with literals that repeat the field initialisers (Http2Options.cs:10-21 and :245-263: 100, 65535, 16384, 64 * 1024, 1), and StreamingOptions.IsDefault compares with constants (StreamingOptions.cs:120-131). UHttpClient uses all three to choose between the shared default transport and a new owned one (UHttpClient.cs:125-141). Http2Options exposes four internal Test*Override properties in the shipping type (Http2Options.cs:26-29) that IsDefault and Clone must track.

**Failure scenario.** options.ConnectionPool.MaxConnectionsPerHost = <default> gives the client its own transport and pool; options.Http2.MaxConcurrentStreams = 100 keeps it on the shared singleton. Changing a default in an initialiser without the matching IsDefault literal would silently give every default client a private transport.

## Suggested fix
Use one mechanism for all three (the explicit-set flag from #184), derive IsDefault from named constants, and move the test overrides to an internal test-configuration object.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] All three option types use one IsDefault mechanism (the explicit-set flag from #184) and derive defaults from named constants
- [ ] Test-only overrides move to an internal test-configuration object and are no longer public
- [ ] a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Core/ fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Core] Header validation is split between UHttpRequest.WithHeader and the transport, and HttpHeaders exposes its internal lists
body:
## Summary
Name and value validation happens in WithHeader and again in the transport, so headers set through other paths (HttpHeaders.Set/Add, clone, interceptors) can carry CR, LF or NUL until the transport rejects them. GetValues and Names hand out internal lists that callers can mutate.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/HttpHeaders.cs:35`

## Problem
UHttpRequest.WithHeader rejects CR/LF in name and value (UHttpRequest.cs:175-187, :577-583) but not invalid token characters, and UHttpRequest.Headers exposes the mutable HttpHeaders (UHttpRequest.cs:47), whose Set/Add/indexer only reject blank names (HttpHeaders.cs:35-64). UHttpClientOptions.DefaultHeaders takes the same unvalidated path. Full validation happens at serialization in the first-party transport (Runtime/Transport/Internal/HttpFieldValidator.cs). HttpHeaders.GetValues returns the internal List<string> typed as IReadOnlyList (HttpHeaders.cs:81-86) and Names returns the live key collection (:108).

**Failure scenario.** request.Headers.Set('X-Id', 'a\r\nInjected: 1') is accepted and fails only at send time with a transport error (or is written as is by a custom IHttpTransport that trusts Core); a caller that keeps the GetValues result sees it change, or gets InvalidOperationException while enumerating Names, when an interceptor mutates the headers.

## Spec reference
9110 section 5.1 and 5.5

## Suggested fix
Validate names (token) and values (no CR, LF, NUL) once in HttpHeaders.Set/Add so every path and every transport gets the same guarantee, and return copies or read-only wrappers from GetValues/Names.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] HttpHeaders.Set/Add validate names as RFC 9110 tokens and reject CR, LF and NUL in values, so every path gets the same guarantee
- [ ] GetValues and Names return copies or read-only wrappers, not internal lists
- [ ] a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Core/ fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Core] HttpHeaders allocates a List<string> and array per header and boxes enumerators on every name walk
body:
## Summary
HttpHeaders stores each header as a List<string>, grows its dictionary from zero capacity and returns boxed enumerators for name walks. Each request and response therefore allocates several objects per header on a hot path.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/HttpHeaders.cs:42`

## Problem
Storage is a Dictionary<string, List<string>> created without capacity (28). Set (42) and Add (62) allocate a List<string> plus its 4-slot array for every header although almost all headers are single-valued; the dictionary re-buckets at 3, 7 and 17 entries; Clone (127-135) repeats all of it. Names (108) returns the KeyCollection as IEnumerable<string>, so each foreach over it (UHttpRequest.CopyHeaders 590, PluginContext.cs:208/847) boxes the enumerator and does a second lookup per name; GetEnumerator (141-148) is an iterator object per enumeration. Each request builds a request HttpHeaders (UHttpRequest.cs:99), a copy of DefaultHeaders (585-600) and a response HttpHeaders, plus more per interceptor copy (core-runtime-05).

**Failure scenario.** A 12-header response and an 8-header request: about 40 List/array objects and 10 dictionary arrays (3-4 KB) per request before any interceptor copy; with three copying interceptors header storage alone is around 10 KB of short-lived garbage per request on the non-generational Boehm GC.

## Suggested fix
Keep the first value inline (entry with a string plus an overflow list only for repeated names) or use a flat insertion-ordered entry list with case-insensitive lookup; add a capacity constructor for Clone and the parsers; expose struct enumerators for names and pairs. Related to but not covered by #120 (parser strings, HTTP/2 header lists).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Single-valued headers are stored without a per-header list (inline first value with overflow only for repeated names, or a flat entry list)
- [ ] HttpHeaders has a capacity constructor used by Clone and the parsers, and struct enumerators for names and pairs
- [ ] Allocations per request for a response with 10 headers are reduced and the measured before/after numbers are recorded in the PR
- [ ] a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Core/ fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `core-runtime-06` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/core.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: performance.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Code facts hold: storage is Dictionary<string, List<string>> without capacity (HttpHeaders.cs:28); Set (42) and Add (62) allocate a List<string> and its array per name; Clone (127-135) repeats that per name; Names (108) returns the KeyCollection as IEnumerable<string>, so foreach over it boxes the enumerator and does a second lookup per name (UHttpRequest.CopyHeaders 590-599, PluginContext.cs:208 and 847); GetEnumerator (141-148) is a compiler-generated iterator. This is a baseline design cost on every request and response rather than a defect, and the quoted totals (3-4 KB, ~10 KB with three copying interceptors) are estimates I did not measure; the order of magnitude is consistent with the code and is doubled by core-runtime-05. Medium only because the project gates allocations at tens of bytes per read (#416, #434); #120 does not cover header storage, so no known issue.

Related: #120, [[R11-core-design-36]], [[R11-core-protocol-07]].

title: [Core] HttpHeaders has no combined field-value accessor; Get and the indexer return only the first field line
body:
## Summary
For list-valued fields sent as several field lines (RFC 9110 section 5.3), Get and the indexer return only the first line, and consumers of such fields rely on it. Values on later lines are silently ignored.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/HttpHeaders.cs:70`

## Problem
Get returns values[0] (HttpHeaders.cs:70-75) and the indexer forwards to it (line 161); the only way to see the other lines is GetValues, and there is no helper that joins them with ", ". The parsers store one value per received line (Http11ResponseParser.cs:302, ConnectReplyReader.cs:130, Http2Connection.ReadLoop.cs:657). RFC 9110 Section 5.3 defines the field value of a list-based field as the lines combined in order. Consumers that read only the first line: DecompressionHandler.TryResolveCompression uses headers.Get("Content-Encoding") (DecompressionHandler.cs:735); ConnectReplyReader uses Headers.Get("Transfer-Encoding") and Headers.Get("Connection") for framing and reuse decisions (ConnectReplyReader.cs:38, 44, 59-61, 163). Applications reading response.Headers.Get("Cache-Control"), "Vary", "Link" or "WWW-Authenticate" get a partial value the same way.

**Failure scenario.** A response carries 'Content-Encoding: gzip' and 'Content-Encoding: deflate' on two lines: only gzip is undone and the caller receives deflate bytes as the body. A proxy 407 reply with 'Connection: keep-alive' and 'Connection: close' on two lines is treated as reusable. A proxy reply with 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' followed by a second Transfer-Encoding line is read as chunked although chunked is not the final coding.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 Sections 5.2 and 5.3

## Suggested fix
Add a combined accessor to HttpHeaders (for example GetCombined(name), joining with ", " and refusing Set-Cookie) and use it in every consumer of a list-based field; document on Get that it is for singleton fields.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] HttpHeaders offers a combined accessor (for example GetCombined(name)) that joins field lines with ", " and refuses Set-Cookie
- [ ] Every consumer of a list-based field uses it, and the Get documentation states it is for singleton fields
- [ ] a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Core/ fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `core-protocol-07` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/core.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: rfc-compat.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: HttpHeaders.Get returns values[0] (HttpHeaders.cs:70-75), the indexer forwards to it (161) and there is no combining accessor; the XML doc on Get does tell callers to use GetValues for multi-value headers (67-68). The affected consumers are real but few and outside Core: DecompressionHandler.TryResolveCompression reads headers.Get("Content-Encoding") (Runtime/Middleware/DecompressionHandler.cs:735), so a second Content-Encoding line is ignored and the body is returned still encoded; ConnectReply uses Get for Transfer-Encoding and Connection (Runtime/Transport/Http1/ConnectReplyReader.cs:38, 44, 59-61, 163). The framing-critical paths already use GetValues: Http11ResponseParser.cs:450 and 601, WebSocketHandshakeValidator.cs:651, CacheInterceptor.cs:318/593/594/722, CacheInterceptor.Variants.cs:19, CacheInterceptor.Parsing.cs:293. So the claim holds for two rare inputs (multi-line Content-Encoding; multi-line Connection/Transfer-Encoding on a non-2xx proxy CONNECT reply), not for the main response path. Severity lowered to low; a GetCombined helper is a reasonable API addition.

Related: [[R11-core-runtime-06]].

title: [Core] HttpMethod is a closed enum, so extension methods cannot be sent
body:
## Summary
HttpMethod is an enum with a fixed set of values, so methods such as PROPFIND, REPORT or QUERY cannot be sent although RFC 9110 section 9.1 allows any token. Customers of WebDAV-style APIs have no way to use the client.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/HttpMethod.cs:6`

## Problem
HttpMethod lists GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, HEAD and OPTIONS (HttpMethod.cs:6-22) and UHttpRequest.Method has that type (UHttpRequest.cs:43); ToUpperString has a fallback for unknown values (:61-67) but no API can create one with a custom token. HasBody (:50-55) has no caller in Runtime/.

**Failure scenario.** A client for WebDAV (PROPFIND, REPORT, MKCOL), HTTP QUERY, PURGE on a CDN, or TRACE cannot be written with this library; changing the type after 1.0 is a breaking change.

## Spec reference
9110 section 9.1

## Suggested fix
Before GA, make the method a small readonly struct or class with static well-known instances and a constructor that validates an RFC 9110 token, keeping IsIdempotent as a property.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The method is a readonly struct or class with static well-known instances and a constructor that validates an RFC 9110 token
- [ ] IsIdempotent remains available as a property and well-known methods keep their current behaviour
- [ ] a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Core/ fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Core] HttpTransportFactory caches a factory exception in its Lazy for the life of the domain
body:
## Summary
The default transport is created through a Lazy, so an exception thrown by the first creation is cached and every later call rethrows it until the domain reloads. A transient failure becomes permanent.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/HttpTransportFactory.cs:57`

## Problem
Every registration builds new Lazy<IHttpTransport>(factory, LazyThreadSafetyMode.ExecutionAndPublication) (57, 78, 114, 259); in that mode Lazy caches an exception thrown by the factory and rethrows it on every Value read (Default, 167). RegisterUnlessCurrent treats the same delegates with a non-null _lazy as current and keeps it (102-116), and DetachCreatedDefault returns null when IsValueCreated is false (253), so the bootstrap's re-registration on Enter Play Mode without domain reload keeps the faulted Lazy as well.

**Failure scenario.** The first HttpTransportFactory.Default read throws inside the factory once (a custom factory missing its configuration, or a transient failure while constructing the transport): every later new UHttpClient() in the process, and in the Editor every later play session until a domain reload, rethrows the same cached exception even after the cause is gone.

## Suggested fix
Create the default under _lock into a null-checked field (no exception caching), or replace the Lazy when its creation faulted.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The default transport is created under the lock into a null-checked field, or the Lazy is replaced when creation faulted, so a later call can succeed after a failed one
- [ ] a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Core/ fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Core] HttpTransportFactory Register/CreateWithOptions overloads silently drop options, and test-only entry points are public
body:
## Summary
The telescoping Register and CreateWithOptions overloads ignore options a registered factory cannot honour, and SetForTesting and Reset are public. A caller can believe options apply when they do not.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/HttpTransportFactory.cs:198`

## Problem
Four delegate shapes are stored (HttpTransportFactory.cs:15-18). CreateWithOptions(tls, pool, http2, streaming) falls back to the three-argument factory (dropping StreamingOptions, :220-224), then to CreateWithBackend (dropping pool and HTTP/2 options, :203-207), then to the default factory (dropping the TLS backend, :179-189). UHttpClient marks the result as owned and disposes it (UHttpClient.cs:130-135, :595-600). Register replaces _lazy without disposing an already created singleton (:50-59). SetForTesting and Reset are public 'for testing only' (:230, :270) although the test assemblies have InternalsVisibleTo.

**Failure scenario.** A transport registered with Register(() => MyTransport.Shared): new UHttpClient(new UHttpClientOptions { TlsBackend = TlsBackend.BouncyCastle, Http2 = { MaxConnectionsPerOrigin = 2 } }) silently gets the default transport with none of the options, and client.Dispose() then disposes the shared instance other clients use.

## Suggested fix
Replace the delegate set with one registration object (for example ITransportFactory { CreateDefault(); Create(TransportCreationOptions) }) and fail with a clear exception when the registered factory cannot honour non-default options; make SetForTesting/Reset internal.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Registration uses one object (for example ITransportFactory with CreateDefault and Create(TransportCreationOptions))
- [ ] A factory that cannot honour non-default options fails with a clear exception instead of dropping them
- [ ] SetForTesting and Reset are internal
- [ ] a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Core/ fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Core] HttpTransportFactory Register, SetForTesting and Reset drop an already created default transport without disposing it
body:
## Summary
Replacing the registration discards the created default transport without disposing it or returning it to the caller, so its sockets and pooled buffers leak. The Reset documentation claims otherwise.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/HttpTransportFactory.cs:270`

## Problem
Register (50-59, 71-80), RegisterUnlessCurrent when not current (108-116), SetForTesting (233-237) and Reset (272-281) overwrite _lazy without handing back a transport the old Lazy created; only DetachCreatedDefault (248-264) returns it. Reset's summary claims it clears any created transport. Default-option clients never dispose the shared default (UHttpClient.cs:137-141). A RawSocketTransport owns a TcpConnectionPool and an Http2ConnectionManager (RawSocketTransport.cs:73-77).

**Failure scenario.** An app calls HttpTransportFactory.Register(customFactory) after a default-options client already sent a request, or a fixture calls Reset() and EnsureRegistered() around each test after touching Default (UHttpRequestBuilderJsonTests.cs:18-33): the previous default transport with its pooled sockets and HTTP/2 loops stays alive, unreachable through the factory, and is never disposed.

## Suggested fix
Have the replacing methods return the detached created default (as DetachCreatedDefault does) so the caller can dispose it, use that internally in Reset and SetForTesting, and correct the Reset documentation.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Register, SetForTesting and Reset return the detached created default (as DetachCreatedDefault does) so the caller can dispose it; Reset and SetForTesting use it internally
- [ ] The Reset documentation is corrected
- [ ] a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Core/ fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Core] IL2CPPCompatibility reports a passing Generic Virtual Methods row without exercising a generic virtual method
body:
## Summary
The compatibility self-check prints a passing row for generic virtual methods but never calls one, so it gives false confidence on IL2CPP builds where such instantiations can be stripped or missing.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/IL2CPPCompatibility.cs:66`

## Problem
CheckGenericVirtualMethods (66-71) boxes an int to IEquatable<int> and calls Equals: an interface call on a closed generic interface, which needs no generic-virtual-method instantiation. CheckAsyncAwait and CheckCancellation exercise types the library could not start without. Validate (19-34) prints "[PASS] Generic Virtual Methods"; its only caller is Tests/Runtime/Platform/PlatformTests.cs:92.

**Failure scenario.** An IL2CPP player run prints the passing row while a real AOT gap (a generic virtual or interface method over a value type, such as a new ValueTask<T> or pool instantiation) would go undetected, and the report is read as device evidence.

## Suggested fix
Exercise the instantiations the library depends on (ValueTask<int> and ValueTask<HttpHeaders> awaits through IResponseBodySource, ArrayPool<T> over the private struct in PluginContext, List<(string, string)>) and a true generic virtual call over a value type, or rename or remove the check.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The check exercises the instantiations the library depends on (ValueTask<int> and ValueTask<HttpHeaders> awaits through IResponseBodySource, ArrayPool<T> over the private struct in PluginContext, List<(string, string)>) and a real generic virtual call over a value type, or the row is renamed or removed
- [ ] The check runs on an IL2CPP player build and the result is recorded (validated on a device or player build)
- [ ] a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Core/ fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Architecture] Core.Internal has become the shared kernel for transport-level code because WebSocket may reference only Core
body:
## Summary
Transport-level helpers such as AbandonedSocketIo live in Core.Internal only so that WebSocket can reach them, which turns Core into a catch-all and blurs the module boundary.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/Internal/AbandonedSocketIo.cs:38`

## Problem

title: [Core] AbandonedSocketIo gate, a libil2cpp workaround, delays new sockets by up to 1 s on Mono
body:
## Summary
AbandonedSocketIo counts abandoned reads and makes new sockets wait up to 1 s in WaitForSettledAsync on every runtime. The gate exists for a libil2cpp descriptor-reuse defect, but on Mono a cancelled or timed-out head read that does not end at socket close delays every new connection in the process, to any host. All Mono targets (Editor, Standalone Mono, Android Mono) are affected.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/Internal/AbandonedSocketIo.cs:134`

## Problem
The class comment (11-29) and #369 attribute the lost-receive defect to libil2cpp's Socket::Close_icall (the Mono runtime's close icall removes the socket from the selector), but Track/Begin (95-126) and WaitForSettledAsync (134-167) are compiled for every runtime and HappyEyeballsConnector.cs:484 awaits the gate before each socket creation. The comment at 57-61 says Mono may never end an abandoned read (#293); such an entry holds the gate for the whole SettleTimeout of 1 s (44).

**Failure scenario.** Mono target (Editor, Standalone Mono, Android Mono): a request times out or is cancelled with a head read pending (Http11ResponseParser.cs:1391) and that read does not end when the socket closes: for the next second every new connection in the process, to any host, waits up to 1 s before its socket is created, although descriptor reuse under a stale selector job cannot happen there.

## Suggested fix
Compile the counting and WaitForSettledAsync only under ENABLE_IL2CPP (keep AbandonOnCancel's observe and dispose behaviour everywhere), or record measurements that show Mono needs it. Confirm by measuring connect latency after a cancelled head read in a Mono player.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The counting and WaitForSettledAsync wait are compiled only under ENABLE_IL2CPP; AbandonOnCancel keeps its observe and dispose behaviour on every runtime, or measurements justify keeping the gate on Mono
- [ ] Connect latency after a cancelled head read in a Mono player is measured and recorded, showing no 1 s delay
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it (gate does not delay a new socket on a non-IL2CPP build path)

title: [Core] ArrayPoolMemoryOwner, SegmentedBuffer and PooledArrayBufferWriter dispose non-atomically, so concurrent Dispose returns an array twice
body:
## Summary
Dispose and TryDetach in these owners read the array field and then return it without an atomic claim. Two threads disposing the same owner (a consumer disposing a message while a connection abort path disposes queued messages) both return the same array to ArrayPool.Shared. Two renters then share one buffer and overwrite each other's data, and the outstanding-buffer accounting is wrong.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/Internal/ArrayPoolMemoryOwner.cs:103`

## Problem
ArrayPoolMemoryOwner.Dispose (101-114) and TryDetach (81-95) read and clear _array without Interlocked; SegmentedBuffer.Dispose (186-193) and PooledArrayBufferWriter.Dispose (188-200) use plain bool flags; ObjectPool.Return (156-184) has no double-return detection. Core's own holders serialize the call (UHttpResponse.cs:304 and UHttpRequestBody.cs:383 use Interlocked.Exchange), but ArrayPoolMemoryOwner is handed out as a general IMemoryOwner<byte> outside Core (PerMessageDeflateExtension.cs:309/379, SyncFlushDeflater.cs:86-91, Http2ResponseBodySource.cs:164, WebSocketConnection.Extensions.cs:142 detaches from owners it did not create).

**Failure scenario.** Two threads dispose the same owner (a consumer disposes a message while a connection abort path disposes queued messages): both read a non-null array and both call ByteArrayPool.Return; ArrayPool.Shared then hands that array to two renters whose data overwrite each other, and the #292 outstanding counter goes negative.

## Suggested fix
Claim the array with Interlocked.Exchange in Dispose and TryDetach, as the other owners already do, and use an int flag with Interlocked in SegmentedBuffer.Dispose.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Dispose and TryDetach in ArrayPoolMemoryOwner and PooledArrayBufferWriter claim the array with Interlocked.Exchange, so the array is returned exactly once
- [ ] SegmentedBuffer.Dispose uses an int flag with Interlocked so concurrent disposal returns each segment once
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Core/ fails before the fix and passes after it (concurrent double Dispose returns each array once; outstanding count returns to zero)

title: [Core] Interceptor ordering is enforced for two pairs only, so Cache outside Redirect or Cookie is accepted
body:
## Summary
InterceptorOrdering validates two pairs and only for first-party types. Configurations such as [CacheInterceptor, RedirectInterceptor] and [CacheInterceptor, CookieInterceptor] are accepted: the first stores a redirected response under the original URL and keeps serving it after the server repoints it, and the second can store a Vary: Cookie response without the cookie in the key. Third-party interceptors cannot declare a role, so they cannot take part in validation.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/Pipeline/InterceptorOrdering.cs:53`

## Problem
InterceptorOrdering.Rules holds Cache-outside-Auth and Concurrency-outside-Retry (InterceptorOrdering.cs:53-70). InterceptorRole.Redirect exists (:13) but no rule uses it for ordering, and there is no Cookie role. IInterceptorRole and InterceptorRole are internal (:10, :23), so a third-party cache or auth interceptor, or a user decorator around a first-party one, has role None and is never checked. RedirectHandler forwards only the final non-3xx response to the outer handler (Runtime/Middleware/RedirectHandler.cs:132-147) and Runtime/Cache contains no redirect handling, so a cache placed outside the redirect interceptor stores the final hop's response under the original URL. The cache builds its Vary key from the request headers it sees (Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.Variants.cs:54), and CookieInterceptor adds Cookie inside it when the cache is outside. Tests/Runtime/Core/InterceptorOrderTests.cs has no case for either order.

**Failure scenario.** Interceptors = [CacheInterceptor, RedirectInterceptor]: GET /latest -> 302 (not cacheable) -> /v2/file 200 max-age=3600 is stored under /latest; after the server repoints /latest the client keeps serving v2 for an hour. Interceptors = [CacheInterceptor, CookieInterceptor]: a response with Vary: Cookie is matched against a request that has no Cookie header yet, so the entry stored for one session is served after the jar switches to another.

## Spec reference
9111 section 3 and 4.1

## Suggested fix
Add Cache-outside-Redirect and Cache-outside-Cookie rules (give CookieInterceptor a role), and make the role contract usable outside the first-party assemblies (public interface or attribute) so custom cache/auth interceptors and decorators take part in validation.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Validation rejects Cache outside Redirect and Cache outside Cookie with the same error type used for the existing pairs; CookieInterceptor has a role
- [ ] The role contract is usable by interceptors outside the first-party assemblies (public interface or attribute), with XML docs
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Core/ fails before the fix and passes after it (each rejected order throws; the valid order is accepted)
- [ ] architecture.md ordering rules are updated

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `core-design-08` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/core.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: architecture.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Rules hold only Cache-outside-Auth and Concurrency-outside-Retry (Runtime/Core/Pipeline/InterceptorOrdering.cs:53-70); InterceptorRole.Redirect is used only for the FollowRedirects warning (UHttpClient.cs:152); IInterceptorRole/InterceptorRole are internal (:10, :23), so a third-party or decorated interceptor has role None. Redirect scenario traced: RedirectHandler forwards only the final non-3xx response to the outer handler (Runtime/Middleware/RedirectHandler.cs:142-156) and CacheStoringHandler stores under the URI and base key captured from the original request (Runtime/Cache/CacheStoringHandler.cs:39-42); rg finds no redirect handling in Runtime/Cache, so Cache outside Redirect stores the final hop's 200 under the original URL for that response's lifetime. The cookie scenario is weaker than stated: a response with Vary: Cookie is not stored unless CachePolicy.AllowVaryCookie is set (Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.cs:614-618, default false), and Set-Cookie responses are not stored by default (:590). Documentation~/Modules/Interceptors.md:51-74 gives the canonical order (Redirect above Cache) but APIReference.md:238 says the client 'rejects unsafe orders', and this one is accepted silently.

title: [Core] ResponseCollectorHandler disposes the staged response before resolving its TaskCompletionSource, so a throwing Dispose hangs SendBufferedAsync
body:
## Summary
On failure paths the collector disposes the staged response first and resolves its completion source afterwards. If Dispose throws (an owner's or a user stream's Dispose), completion was already claimed, the exception is lost in an unobserved continuation, and the TaskCompletionSource is never completed.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/Pipeline/ResponseCollectorHandler.cs:71`

## Problem
OnResponseError (68-79), Fail (90-111) and Cancel (119-123) claim completion (TryClaimCompletion sets _completionClaimed), then call stagedResponse?.Dispose(), and only afterwards resolve _tcs. UHttpResponse.Dispose runs the detached owner's Dispose and the attached release callbacks (UHttpResponse.cs:304-324: ReleaseResponseHold -> TryCompleteLease -> content.Dispose -> the caller's Stream.Dispose once the request was disposed). Fail and Cancel run inside the discarded ContinueWith task of BufferedDispatchBridge.cs:61-102. architecture.md requires every completion source to stay resolved when a downstream callback throws.

**Failure scenario.** A response is staged, the dispatch then faults (a late fault after the body) and disposing the staged response throws (an owner's or a user stream's Dispose): completion is already claimed, the exception disappears in the unobserved continuation, _tcs is never completed and SendBufferedAsync never returns.

## Suggested fix
Resolve the TaskCompletionSource first, or dispose the staged response in a try/finally that always resolves it, in all three methods.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] In all three failure methods the TaskCompletionSource is resolved first, or the dispose runs in try/finally that always resolves it
- [ ] A throwing Dispose never leaves SendBufferedAsync pending
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Core/ fails before the fix and passes after it (staged response whose Dispose throws, late fault after the body; the task completes with the original error)

title: [Core] Buffered collection copies every body byte twice through a scratch array
body:
## Summary
The collector reads into a scratch array and then copies into the SegmentedBuffer. A 20 MB buffered HTTP/1.1 download performs an extra 20 MB of memcpy and 1280 extra loop iterations compared with reading straight into the tail segment.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/Pipeline/ResponseCollectorHandler.cs:175`

## Problem
For a source that cannot be detached CollectAsync rents a 16 KB scratch array (175), reads into it (180) and copies each chunk into the SegmentedBuffer (186), because SegmentedBuffer only exposes GetWriteSpan (Span, SegmentedBuffer.cs:91-99) and ReadAsync needs Memory. The TryGetBufferedData branch (164-171) likewise copies an already buffered body into new segments.

**Failure scenario.** A 20 MB buffered HTTP/1.1 download performs an extra 20 MB of memcpy and 1280 extra loop iterations compared with reading straight into the tail segment.

## Suggested fix
Add GetWriteMemory(sizeHint) to SegmentedBuffer (PooledSegment already owns the array) and read directly into it with Advance; drop the scratch rental.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] SegmentedBuffer exposes GetWriteMemory(sizeHint) with Advance and the collector reads directly into it; the scratch rental is removed
- [ ] Body bytes are copied once between the transport read and the buffer; a measurement on a 20 MB body shows the extra copy and iterations gone

title: [Core] Buffered collector discards HTTP/2 response trailers whenever the body source can be detached
body:
## Summary
When an HTTP/2 response arrives as HEADERS, DATA and trailing HEADERS in one flight, SendBufferedAsync detaches the body and returns a UHttpResponse with empty Trailers. The same response read slowly, or through SendStreamingAsync, has the trailers, so the result depends on timing. Trailers such as grpc-status, digests or Server-Timing are lost.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/Pipeline/ResponseCollectorHandler.cs:208`

## Problem
CollectAsync tries body.TryDetachBufferedBody first (ResponseCollectorHandler.cs:159). On that path it never asks for trailers (line 190: 'if (!detached) trailers = await body.GetTrailersAsync') and builds the response with 'trailers: HttpHeaders.Empty' (line 208). DetachedBufferedBody carries no trailers. The Core sources refuse to detach when trailers exist (BufferedResponseBodySource.cs:38, SegmentedResponseBodySource.cs:71), but Http2ResponseBodySource.TryDetachBufferedBody (Runtime/Transport/Http2/Http2ResponseBodySource.cs:90-110) only requires the stream to be complete and the trailers task to be completed without fault; it does not check that the trailers are empty. The read loop sets the trailers and then completes the body (Http2Connection.ReadLoop.cs:694-697), and OnResponseStartAsync runs from a queued thread-pool work item (Http2Stream.cs:288, 636-655), so for a small response the read loop has usually processed DATA and the trailing HEADERS before the collector runs. No test asserts buffered HTTP/2 trailers (only HTTP/1.1: RawSocketTransportTests.cs:2275).

**Failure scenario.** An HTTP/2 server answers with HEADERS, one DATA frame and trailing HEADERS (grpc-status, a digest, Server-Timing) in one flight. SendBufferedAsync returns a UHttpResponse whose Trailers is empty; the same response read slowly (or through SendStreamingAsync) has the trailers. The result depends on a race between the read loop and the queued response-start callback.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 Section 6.5; RFC 9113 Section 8.1

## Suggested fix
Make the detach contract carry trailers: either add trailers to DetachedBufferedBody and pass them to UHttpResponse, or have the collector read GetTrailersAsync before detaching and have Http2ResponseBodySource refuse to detach when its trailers are not empty. Add a deterministic test with a completed HTTP/2 stream that has trailers.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] UHttpResponse.Trailers from SendBufferedAsync contains the HTTP/2 trailers regardless of whether the body source was detached (RFC 9113 section 8.1)
- [ ] The detach contract carries trailers (DetachedBufferedBody holds them), or the collector reads GetTrailersAsync before detaching and Http2ResponseBodySource refuses to detach when trailers are pending
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Core/ fails before the fix and passes after it or Tests/Runtime/Transport/ with a complete HEADERS, DATA, trailing HEADERS flight delivered in one read

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `core-protocol-02` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/core.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: protocol-impl.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. ResponseCollectorHandler.cs:159 tries TryDetachBufferedBody first; on that path line 190 skips GetTrailersAsync and line 208 builds the response with trailers: HttpHeaders.Empty. The Core sources honour the implied contract (BufferedResponseBodySource.cs:38 refuses when _trailers.Count != 0), and Tests/Runtime/Pipeline/BufferedDispatchBridgeTests.cs:73 (DetachedBufferedBody_SkipsTrailersAndSourceDispose) pins 'detached means no trailers'. Http2ResponseBodySource.TryDetachBufferedBody (Runtime/Transport/Http2/Http2ResponseBodySource.cs:94-110) only requires terminal state Completed and a completed, non-faulted trailers task; it never checks that the result is empty. The read loop sets the trailers and then completes the body (Http2Connection.ReadLoop.cs:694-697 -> Http2Stream.cs:452-454 SetTrailers, 492-494 Complete), and response start is a queued thread-pool item (Http2Stream.cs:288), so when DATA and trailing HEADERS are processed before the collector runs the source detaches and the trailers are dropped; otherwise the read path returns them. Result is race dependent, as stated. No buffered HTTP/2 trailer test exists (only the streaming one, Http2ConnectionTests.StreamingResponses.cs:17-76). HTTP/1.1 is not affected (Http11ResponseBodySource.cs:99-121 detaches only empty bodies). The fix belongs in the Transport source and/or the Core detach contract.

title: [Core] Buffered body size limit is a retryable NetworkError and UHttpErrorType.Cancelled is never produced
body:
## Summary
Exceeding MaxBufferedResponseBodySize is reported as a NetworkError, which IsRetryable() treats as retryable. Code that retries on that check re-downloads up to 100 MB by default on every attempt for a response that will always be too large. UHttpErrorType.Cancelled is public but nothing produces it, so code that switches on it never runs.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/Pipeline/ResponseCollectorHandler.cs:278`

## Problem
ThrowIfOverBufferedLimit raises UHttpErrorType.NetworkError for a local policy limit (ResponseCollectorHandler.cs:274-283); UHttpError.IsRetryable returns true for NetworkError (UHttpError.cs:72-74). UHttpErrorType has no member for limits or protocol violations (:9-31). UHttpErrorType.Cancelled (:24) is never constructed in Runtime/ (only compared in Runtime/Testing/MockTransport.cs:259 and RecordReplayTransport.cs:521); cancellation surfaces as OperationCanceledException (Internal/CancellationClassification.cs).

**Failure scenario.** Application code that retries while error.IsRetryable() re-downloads up to MaxBufferedResponseBodySize (100 MB by default) on every attempt for a response that will always be too large; code that switches on Cancelled never runs.

## Suggested fix
Add a non-retryable error type for local limits (for example ResponseTooLarge or a general LimitExceeded) and use it here; remove or obsolete Cancelled.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A non-retryable error type for local limits (for example ResponseTooLarge or LimitExceeded) is raised for the buffered size limit and IsRetryable() returns false for it
- [ ] UHttpErrorType.Cancelled is removed or marked obsolete, or produced where cancellation is surfaced; the choice is documented

title: [Core] Core references UnityEngine only for PlatformInfo code that tests call, and cannot be built or tested engine-free
body:
## Summary
Core carries a UnityEngine reference for platform detection used mainly by tests, and the editor check needs a NoInlining workaround. The plain-.NET harness relies on JIT-time binding failure caught by a bare catch in UHttpClient, and the default diagnostics sink silently fails there.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/PlatformInfo.cs:1`

## Problem
UnityEngine is used in Core at PlatformInfo.cs:1-66 (Application.platform/isEditor/unityVersion), PlatformConfig.cs:83-88 (Debug.Log in LogPlatformInfo), UHttpClient.cs:829 (Application.isPlaying, Editor only) and TurboDiagnostics.cs:126-138 (Debug.LogWarning, RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod). PlatformInfo is referenced only by PlatformConfig.LogPlatformInfo and IL2CPPCompatibility, and neither has a caller in Runtime/ (only Tests/Runtime/Platform). PlatformConfig's defaults are #if constants. UHttpClient.cs:825-829 documents that the engine call must sit in its own NoInlining method so the Tools~ harnesses on plain .NET survive the failed binding. TurboHTTP.Core.asmdef:13 therefore keeps noEngineReferences false, unlike Transport, JSON and WebSocket.

**Failure scenario.** Core cannot be compiled or unit-tested engine-free; the plain-.NET harness relies on JIT-time binding failure being caught by a bare catch (UHttpClient.cs:812-815), and the default diagnostics sink silently fails there.

## Suggested fix
Move PlatformInfo, IL2CPPCompatibility and LogPlatformInfo to the test or Unity assembly, inject the default diagnostics sink and the play-mode check from the bootstrap (TurboHTTP.Complete/Unity already register transport and JSON), then set noEngineReferences true.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] PlatformInfo, IL2CPPCompatibility and LogPlatformInfo move to the test or Unity assembly
- [ ] The default diagnostics sink and the play-mode check are injected from the bootstrap (TurboHTTP.Complete or Unity)
- [ ] TurboHTTP.Core sets noEngineReferences true and builds, and the bare catch in UHttpClient is removed

title: [Core] Plugin capability model can be escaped through OptionsSnapshot and post-forwarding mutation
body:
## Summary
A plugin declared ObserveRequests or None can read credentials (proxy password, default Authorization header), the transport and all interceptors through context.OptionsSnapshot during InitializeAsync. It can also add a header to every outgoing request from OnRequestStart after the read-only guard has forwarded, and no PluginException is raised. The guard suggests a restriction it does not provide.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/PluginContext.cs:39`

## Problem
(1) PluginContext.OptionsSnapshot (line 39) is not capability-gated. UHttpClient passes _options.Clone() (UHttpClient.cs:236-241) and Clone copies DefaultHeaders, clones Proxy with its NetworkCredential password, and shares the Transport reference and the interceptor instances (UHttpClientOptions.cs:180-202). A plugin with PluginCapabilities.None therefore reads default Authorization headers and the proxy password, can dispatch through OptionsSnapshot.Transport around the whole pipeline, and can reach the auth, cookie and cache interceptor objects. (2) The read-only guard compares hashes at fixed points: ObservedHandler.OnRequestStart records the request hash, the plugin handler forwards, InvocationGuard.OnRequestStart compares (lines 355-360, 632-636). A plugin handler that forwards first and then calls request.Headers.Set(...) is not seen; the transport calls OnRequestStart before it serializes (RawSocketTransport.cs:158, 175), so the header reaches the wire, and GuardedNextAsync's finally then recaptures the baseline (lines 344-349) before the post-dispatch check (line 299). The same works for response headers: forward OnResponseStartAsync, then mutate the shared HttpHeaders object that UHttpResponse keeps. (3) Metadata values are hashed with GetHashCode (lines 220-236), so mutable reference values such as ProxySettings change unseen. (4) RequestContext.SetState/UpdateRequest are open to every plugin (RequestContext.cs:127-143), including the transport's own keys (TransportBehaviorFlags). (5) HandleErrors is only enforced for exceptions thrown out of next (lines 427-441); transport failures arrive through OnResponseError (RawSocketTransport.cs:178-181), which a plugin with MutateResponses can turn into a response. Tests cover replacement, redispatch and pre-forward mutation only (Tests/Runtime/Core/PluginInterceptorCapabilityTests.cs).

**Failure scenario.** A third-party plugin declared as ObserveRequests (or None) reads context.OptionsSnapshot.Proxy.Credentials.Password and the default Authorization header during InitializeAsync, or adds a header to every outgoing request from its OnRequestStart after forwarding; the client reports no PluginException and GetRegisteredPlugins still lists it as read-only.

## Suggested fix
Decide what the model promises. If it is a guard against accidental misuse, say so in the XML docs and drop the hash machinery that suggests more. If it is meant to restrict plugins: give OptionsSnapshot a redacted view (no Transport, no interceptor instances, no credentials or default headers unless a capability grants them), hand read-only plugins a frozen request/headers view instead of comparing hashes after the fact, and gate RequestContext mutation.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The promise of the capability model is decided and stated in XML docs: either an accident guard only, with the hash machinery that implies more removed, or a restriction
- [ ] If restricting: OptionsSnapshot is a redacted view (no Transport, no interceptor instances, no credentials or default headers unless a capability grants them) and mutations after forwarding raise PluginException
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Core/ fails before the fix and passes after it (plugin without the capability cannot read credentials or mutate after forwarding)

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `core-protocol-05` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/core.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: security.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Each sub-claim checks out in the code: (1) PluginContext.OptionsSnapshot (PluginContext.cs:39) is ungated and the clone carries DefaultHeaders, the Proxy clone with its credentials, the Transport reference and the interceptor instances (UHttpClientOptions.cs:180-202). (2) The request guard compares only before dispatch and after the wrapped call (PluginContext.cs:320, 299) and GuardedNextAsync's finally re-captures the baseline (344-349), so a mutation made by the plugin's handler after it forwarded OnRequestStart is absorbed; the transport serialises after OnRequestStart (RawSocketTransport.cs:158, 175) and may even pass a copy the guard never baselines (PrepareEffectiveRequest, 397-413). (3) Metadata values are hashed with GetHashCode (231). (4) RequestContext.UpdateRequest/SetState are public and ungated (RequestContext.cs:127-143). (5) With MutateResponses RecordForwarded returns early (529-530), so OnResponseError can be turned into a response without HandleErrors. Tests cover replacement, redispatch and pre-forward mutation only. Severity lowered from medium: plugins are in-process code registered by the application, nothing in the XML docs or Documentation~ promises a sandbox (IHttpPlugin.cs:7-9 says only 'capability-scoped registrations'), and a managed plugin can bypass any such guard anyway. The valid point is design: the hash machinery is costly (core-runtime-04) and suggests a guarantee it does not give, so the contract should be stated as a misuse guard or tightened. #182 tracks only the file's size.

title: [Core] PluginContext stays usable after InitializeAsync, so late RegisterInterceptor mutates the list without a lock and skips ordering validation
body:
## Summary
A plugin that keeps the context can call RegisterInterceptor later. The registration list is mutated without the lock, and the interceptor is installed later without ordering validation, for example an AuthInterceptor appearing inside CacheInterceptor when another plugin is unregistered, an order the constructor rejects.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/PluginContext.cs:45`

## Problem
RegisterPluginAsync passes the lambda 'interceptor => contributedInterceptors.Add(interceptor)' to the context (UHttpClient.cs:235-241) and then stores the same List as PluginRegistration.Interceptors (:247-250, :71). PluginContext has no sealed/completed state (PluginContext.cs:45-80). A later call adds to that List outside _pluginLock while BuildCombinedInterceptors_NoLock may be iterating it (UHttpClient.cs:705-729). The pipeline is not rebuilt, so the interceptor is inactive until another plugin registers or unregisters; UnregisterPluginAsync rebuilds through RebuildPipelineSnapshot_NoLock, which does not call InterceptorOrdering.FindViolation (:693-703), and RegisterPluginAsync would attribute a resulting violation to the unrelated candidate plugin (:268-283). No test in Tests/Runtime/Core/PluginRegistryTests.cs covers a call after initialization.

**Failure scenario.** A plugin keeps the context and registers an AuthInterceptor lazily on first use. Nothing happens until some other plugin is unregistered; then the auth interceptor silently appears inside the base CacheInterceptor, the order the constructor rejects (#55).

## Suggested fix
Seal the context when InitializeAsync completes (throw InvalidOperationException from RegisterInterceptor afterwards) and hand the registration an immutable copy of the contributions.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] PluginContext is sealed when InitializeAsync completes; RegisterInterceptor afterwards throws InvalidOperationException
- [ ] The registration receives an immutable copy of the contributions
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Core/ fails before the fix and passes after it (late registration throws and no interceptor is installed)

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `core-design-09` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/core.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: architecture.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. The context's callback adds to contributedInterceptors (Runtime/Core/UHttpClient.cs:235-241) and the same List instance becomes PluginRegistration.Interceptors (:247-250, :71). PluginContext has no completed state (Runtime/Core/PluginContext.cs:45-80), so a call after InitializeAsync appends outside _pluginLock while BuildCombinedInterceptors_NoLock may index the list (:705-729); it takes effect only at the next rebuild, and RebuildPipelineSnapshot_NoLock (:693-703) does not call InterceptorOrdering.FindViolation. Downgraded: it needs a plugin that keeps the context beyond initialization, which the type's summary ('provided during plugin initialization') does not invite, and there is no first-party plugin. The fix (seal the context, copy the list) is small.

title: [Docs] Plugin example registers an interceptor with Capabilities.None and body docs call Expect: 100-continue unimplemented
body:
## Summary
The plugin example registers an interceptor with PluginCapabilities.None, which raises a PluginException at registration, so a customer who copies it fails. The request-body docs say Expect: 100-continue is not implemented although WithExpectContinue exists.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/PluginContext.cs:56`

## Problem
RegisterInterceptor throws PluginException('Plugin does not have interceptor capabilities.') unless the plugin has ObserveRequests, ReadOnlyMonitoring, MutateRequests, MutateResponses or HandleErrors (PluginContext.cs:50-62). title: [Core] Plugin system (about 1,360 lines) has no first-party consumer, is rooted by public API and its capability checks are not a real boundary
body:
## Summary
PluginContext, IHttpPlugin and the plugin region of UHttpClient total about 1,360 lines of Core, and nothing in Runtime/ or Samples~/ implements or registers a plugin. Because PluginContext and RegisterPluginAsync are public, UnityLinker keeps the whole machinery at Managed Stripping Level Minimal and Low. The mutation checks hash the full request body byte by byte, and the checks are not an enforceable security boundary. Every player pays the size cost and every plugin user pays the hashing cost.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/PluginContext.cs:96`

## Problem
rg finds no IHttpPlugin implementation or RegisterPluginAsync call in Runtime/ or Samples~/ (only UHttpClient.cs, IHttpPlugin.cs and docs). PluginContext.cs is 885 lines, IHttpPlugin.cs 79, and the plugin region of UHttpClient.cs about 400 (:53-79, :211-372, :514-729). PluginContext and UHttpClient.RegisterPluginAsync are public, so UnityLinker keeps the whole capability machinery at Managed Stripping Level Minimal and Low. Cost when used: RequestMutationSignature.Capture reads request.Content.GetHashCode() (PluginContext.cs:150), and BufferedRequestBody/OwnedMemoryRequestBody override GetHashCode with a byte-wise hash of the whole body (UHttpRequestBody.cs:328-331, :391-397, :242-254). For a plugin without MutateRequests/MutateResponses, Capture runs at PluginContext.cs:270, :320 (via :396), :634, :358, :348 and :299: six passes plus header and metadata hashes. Enforcement is by 32-bit hash comparison and trusts in-process code: OptionsSnapshot (PluginContext.cs:39) gives every plugin, whatever its capabilities, the Transport instance, the interceptor instances, DefaultHeaders and Proxy credentials (UHttpClientOptions.Clone, UHttpClientOptions.cs:180-202), and the mutation baseline is re-captured after each downstream dispatch (:344-349).

**Failure scenario.** A project registers a ReadOnlyMonitoring plugin: each 10 MB upload is hashed about 60 MB byte by byte on the calling threads. A project that never registers a plugin still ships the code at the default IL2CPP stripping level. Estimate (not measured): ~1.3k source lines, tens of KB of IL.

## Suggested fix
Move plugin hosting and CapabilityEnforcedInterceptor into an optional assembly (for example TurboHTTP.Plugins) that composes the client through an internal pipeline hook, or reduce it to a named interceptor bundle with async init/shutdown. If capability checks stay, drop the content-hash GetHashCode overrides and compare body identity only.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Plugin hosting and CapabilityEnforcedInterceptor live in an optional assembly (or are reduced to a named interceptor bundle), so a build that does not use plugins does not link them
- [ ] Capability checks no longer compute content-hash GetHashCode over request bodies; body identity (reference and length) is compared instead
- [ ] Core public API baseline and docs are updated for the moved or removed types
- [ ] Regression test under Tests/Runtime/Core/ covers plugin registration, capability enforcement and shutdown through the new hosting

For an interceptor without MutateRequests and MutateResponses, RequestMutationSignature.Capture runs at PluginContext.cs:270, :320 (via :396), :634 and :358 (ResponseEventSignature.ForRequestStart -> ComputeHash, :792-796), :348 and :299: six full-body passes per request; the :358 pass runs even with MutateResponses because the argument is evaluated before RecordForwarded's early return. title: [Core] Plugin capability guard hashes the whole buffered request body about six times per request and re-wraps the interceptor on every request
body:
## Summary
RequestMutationSignature.Capture calls request.Content.GetHashCode(), which for BufferedRequestBody and OwnedMemoryRequestBody is a byte-at-a-time loop over the entire body, and also hashes all headers. For a guarded plugin this capture runs about six times per request, and the plugin interceptor is wrapped again on every request. A 50 MB upload costs about 300 MB of byte-wise hashing per guarded plugin.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/PluginContext.cs:150`

## Problem
RequestMutationSignature.Capture stores request.Content.GetHashCode() (150). BufferedRequestBody and OwnedMemoryRequestBody override GetHashCode with ComputeStableHash, a byte-at-a-time loop over the entire body (UHttpRequestBody.cs:242-254, 328-331, 391-397); Capture also hashes every header name and value (200-218). For a plugin without the full capability set one request runs Capture in the InvocationGuard constructor (270), the GuardedNextAsync pre-check (320 -> 396), ObservedHandler.OnRequestStart (634), InvocationGuard.OnRequestStart (358; the argument is computed before RecordForwarded's early return at 529, so MutateResponses plugins pay it too), the GuardedNextAsync finally (348) and the post-dispatch check (299). InvokeAsync calls _owner._inner.Wrap(GuardedNextAsync) per request (275), although the chain is documented as built once (architecture.md, Request pipeline), and allocates an InvocationGuard, two lock objects, an ObservedHandler, an ObservedBodySource and an ArrayPool<ResponseEventSignature> rental each time.

**Failure scenario.** A read-only monitoring plugin (ObserveRequests) is registered and the app uploads a 50 MB buffered body: about 300 MB of byte-wise hashing runs per request and per guarded plugin (hundreds of milliseconds on a phone) before and after the send; an interceptor that allocates or registers state in Wrap does so for every request.

## Suggested fix
Do not hash body bytes for the mutation check: compare the content reference (already compared) and length, or cache one hash per body instance. Build the forwarded signature only when the response guard is active, and wrap the inner interceptor once per pipeline build, passing per-request guard state through the handler.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A guarded plugin no longer hashes request body bytes: the mutation check compares content reference and length, or uses one cached hash per body instance
- [ ] The forwarded signature is built only when the response guard is active, and the inner interceptor is wrapped once per pipeline build
- [ ] Measured target: body bytes hashed per request for a read-only plugin is 0 (was about 6x body length)
- [ ] Regression test under Tests/Runtime/Core/ fails before the fix: it counts GetHashCode body passes or Wrap calls for a guarded plugin and asserts none per request

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `core-runtime-04` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/core.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: performance.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. RequestMutationSignature captures request.Content.GetHashCode() (PluginContext.cs:150); BufferedRequestBody and OwnedMemoryRequestBody override GetHashCode with a byte-wise loop over the whole body (UHttpRequestBody.cs:242-254, 328-331, 391-397), and every capture also hashes all header names and values (200-218). For a guarded plugin (anything short of MutateRequests + MutateResponses + HandleErrors + AllowRedispatch, PluginContext.cs:64-79) one request captures in: the InvocationGuard constructor (270, unconditional), the pre-dispatch check (320 -> 396, without MutateRequests), ObservedHandler.OnRequestStart (634, without MutateResponses), InvocationGuard.OnRequestStart (358, argument built before RecordForwarded's early return at 529, so unconditional), the GuardedNextAsync finally (348, unconditional) and the post-dispatch check (299). That is six full-body hashes for an ObserveRequests/ReadOnlyMonitoring plugin and three even with both mutate flags but no redispatch. InvokeAsync also calls _owner._inner.Wrap(GuardedNextAsync) per request (275) and allocates the guard, two lock objects, the ObservedHandler/ObservedBodySource and an ArrayPool rental (554). Opt-in path (only with a partially capable plugin) and negligible for small bodies, so medium, not higher.

title: [Core] ProxyBypassMatcher, ProxyEnvironmentResolver, InterceptorPipeline and UHttpClient.Transport are public implementation details; HappyEyeballsOptions is in the Transport namespace
body:
## Summary
Several public Core types have no consumer outside Core, so their shape would be frozen at 1.0 for no benefit. HappyEyeballsOptions is declared in TurboHTTP.Transport.Connection inside the Core assembly, so users import a Transport namespace to configure a Core option. UHttpClient.Transport exposes a disposable transport that every default client shares.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/ProxySettings.cs:68`

## Problem
ProxyBypassMatcher (ProxySettings.cs:68) and ProxyEnvironmentResolver (:225) are public static classes with no user outside Runtime/Core (rg over Runtime/, Samples~/, Documentation~/). InterceptorPipeline is public (Pipeline/InterceptorPipeline.cs:9) and only constructed in UHttpClient. HappyEyeballsOptions is declared in namespace TurboHTTP.Transport.Connection inside the Core assembly (HappyEyeballsOptions.cs:3; ConnectionPoolOptions.cs:2 imports it), the one entry in Tools~/ci/api-baseline/core-public-types.txt outside TurboHTTP.Core. UHttpClient.Transport (UHttpClient.cs:51) returns the transport, which for default options is the process-wide HttpTransportFactory.Default singleton. ProxySettings.Clone pulls System.Linq into Core for one ToArray (ProxySettings.cs:3, :40).

**Failure scenario.** Public surface that must be kept stable at 1.0 for no consumer; client.Transport.Dispose() tears down the transport every default client shares; users must import a Transport namespace to configure a Core option.

## Suggested fix
Make the two proxy helpers and InterceptorPipeline internal, move HappyEyeballsOptions to TurboHTTP.Core (or the type to Transport with a Core-side DTO), and return a non-disposable view or remove the Transport property.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ProxyBypassMatcher, ProxyEnvironmentResolver and InterceptorPipeline are internal
- [ ] HappyEyeballsOptions is in the TurboHTTP.Core namespace (or a Core-side DTO replaces it) and the API baseline is updated

title: [Proxy] Proxy bypass matching exists twice with different grammars: ProxyBypassMatcher and WebSocketProxySettings.ShouldBypass
body:
## Summary
Core's ProxyBypassMatcher supports exact names, .domain, *.domain, CIDR, port suffixes and bracketed IPv6, while WebSocketProxySettings.ShouldBypass supports only exact names and *.domain. Both expose a property called BypassList. The same list therefore bypasses the proxy for HTTP requests but not for WebSocket connections.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/ProxySettings.cs:100`

## Problem
ProxyBypassMatcher.MatchesRule supports exact names, '.domain' (apex and subdomains), '*.domain', CIDR, ':port' suffixes and bracketed IPv6 (ProxySettings.cs:100-153, documented at :13-26). WebSocketProxySettings.ShouldBypass supports only exact names and '*.domain' (Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketProxySettings.cs:83-112). Both properties are named BypassList, the WebSocket assembly references Core, and ProxyBypassMatcher is public, yet it has no caller outside Core. The WebSocket side also has its own credentials type and no environment-variable resolution.

**Failure scenario.** BypassList = { '.corp.example', '10.0.0.0/8', 'localhost:8080' } keeps HTTP requests to those hosts off the proxy but sends WebSocket connections to the same hosts through it.

## Suggested fix
Have WebSocketProxySettings delegate to ProxyBypassMatcher.IsBypassed (same grammar, one test suite), or share one immutable proxy-settings type between the two stacks.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] WebSocketProxySettings.ShouldBypass delegates to one shared matcher (ProxyBypassMatcher.IsBypassed or a shared settings type)
- [ ] A BypassList of .corp.example, 10.0.0.0/8 and localhost:8080 bypasses the proxy for WebSocket connections exactly as for HTTP
- [ ] Regression test under Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ fails before the fix and covers the full rule grammar

title: [Proxy] NO_PROXY ignores the '*' wildcard and treats a bare domain as an exact host, unlike curl, wget and Go
body:
## Summary
ProxyBypassMatcher.MatchesRule falls through to an exact string comparison for a lone '*', which never matches, and a bare domain like example.com matches only that host. In curl, wget and Go, '*' disables the proxy for every host and a bare domain also matches its subdomains. Machines with NO_PROXY=* or NO_PROXY=corp.example still send internal requests to the proxy.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/ProxySettings.cs:152`

## Problem
MatchesRule (ProxySettings.cs:100-153) handles '*.suffix', '.suffix', CIDR and exact names. A rule of '*' is none of these and falls to string.Equals(host, "*") (line 152), which never matches. A bare 'example.com' is an exact match only (documented at lines 16-17), while the leading-dot form is described as 'curl NO_PROXY semantics'; in curl, wget and Go a bare domain also matches its subdomains and '*' disables the proxy for every host. The same matcher serves NO_PROXY/no_proxy (lines 254-258). The tests cover '.internal.test', 'localhost' and '*.corp.test' only (Tests/Runtime/Core/ProxyBypassRulesTests.cs:80, 98). #173 (closed) fixed the apex case, not these.

**Failure scenario.** A developer or CI machine has HTTP_PROXY set and NO_PROXY=* (or NO_PROXY=corp.example expecting api.corp.example to be direct). Every request, including http:// requests to internal hosts, is still sent to the proxy in absolute-form with its headers, or fails because the proxy cannot reach the internal host.

## Suggested fix
Treat a lone '*' as 'bypass everything', and for entries that come from the environment variable match a bare domain as the domain and its subdomains (keep the exact-match rule for the programmatic BypassList if that is intended, and document the difference). Add tests for both.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A lone '*' in NO_PROXY bypasses the proxy for every host
- [ ] A bare domain taken from NO_PROXY/no_proxy matches the domain and its subdomains; the programmatic BypassList behaviour is kept or documented
- [ ] Documentation states the difference between the environment variable and BypassList
- [ ] Regression test under Tests/Runtime/Core/ fails before the fix and covers '*', bare domain and subdomain

## Context

Verifier note: MatchesRule (ProxySettings.cs:100-153) handles '*.suffix', '.suffix', CIDR and exact names; a lone '*' matches none of the prefixes and falls to string.Equals(host, "*") at 152, which never matches. A bare name is exact-match only, which is documented (16-17) and applied to NO_PROXY too (25, 254-258); curl and Go treat a bare domain as the domain plus subdomains and '*' as 'no proxy for anything', while line 17 claims 'curl NO_PROXY semantics' for the dotted form only. Tests cover '.internal.test', 'localhost', '*.corp.test' (Tests/Runtime/Core/ProxyBypassRulesTests.cs:80, 98; ProxySettingsTests.cs:43); none for '*' or a bare parent domain. #173 (closed) fixed the wildcard apex and CIDR docs, not these. title: [Core] ProxySettings is stored by reference in public request metadata, so options are mutable after construction and proxy credentials reach every interceptor
body:
## Summary
The client clones its options once, but ProxyEnvironmentResolver.Resolve returns that same ProxySettings instance and ApplyDefaultMetadata stores it in each request's public Metadata. ProxySettings has public setters, including Credentials with the password and AllowPlaintextProxyAuth. Any interceptor or observe-only plugin can change the proxy for all later requests of the client and can read the proxy password.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/ProxySettings.cs:238`

## Problem
UHttpClient clones the options once (UHttpClient.cs:95). ProxyEnvironmentResolver.Resolve returns the configured instance itself when it applies ('return configured', ProxySettings.cs:234-238) and ApplyDefaultMetadata stores that instance in each request's metadata (UHttpClient.cs:756-758). UHttpRequest.Metadata is public (UHttpRequest.cs:65) and ProxySettings has public setters for Address, Credentials (NetworkCredential with the password), BypassList and AllowPlaintextProxyAuth (ProxySettings.cs:11-30). The plugin mutation guard hashes metadata values by reference (PluginContext.cs:231), so it does not see such a change. This contradicts the 'Shared config: never mutate caller-owned or static configuration per request: clone it' contract in Development~/docs/agents/architecture.md.

**Failure scenario.** Any interceptor or ObserveRequests-only plugin runs ((ProxySettings)request.Metadata[RequestMetadataKeys.ProxySettings]).AllowPlaintextProxyAuth = true (or changes Address): the change applies to every later request of that client, and the same reference exposes the proxy password to code that was only meant to observe requests.

## Suggested fix
Store an immutable resolved-proxy value in metadata (internal sealed type with read-only fields, built once per client), or keep the proxy out of public metadata and let the transport read it from a typed internal slot on the request/context.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Request metadata no longer exposes a mutable ProxySettings; an immutable resolved-proxy value or an internal typed slot is used

title: [Core] Unsupported proxy scheme in HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY makes every request builder call throw synchronously by default
body:
## Summary
With UHttpClientOptions.Proxy unset, ProxyEnvironmentResolver reads the environment on every CreateRequest and throws UHttpException(InvalidRequest) when the value is not http://. The exception leaves client.Get() and CreateRequest synchronously instead of the awaited send. A player with HTTPS_PROXY=socks5://... that never configured a proxy crashes callers that only wrap the send.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/ProxySettings.cs:260`

## Problem
With UHttpClientOptions.Proxy left null, ProxyEnvironmentResolver.Resolve reads the environment on every CreateRequest (ProxySettings.cs:241-257) and throws UHttpException(InvalidRequest) when the value is not http:// (:260-268). The call sits in ApplyDefaultMetadata, so the exception leaves client.Get()/Post()/CreateRequest (UHttpClient.cs:180-190), not the awaited send. #173 chose a typed exception over the raw ArgumentException; its other accepted option (ignore with a diagnostic) was not taken, and the throw site is the builder, where callers do not expect network-configuration errors.

**Failure scenario.** A player runs the game with HTTPS_PROXY=socks5://127.0.0.1:1080 (or https://corp-proxy:8443). The game never configured a proxy, yet every client.Get(url) throws before any await; code that wraps only the send in try/catch crashes its caller, and the developer can only fix it by shipping UseEnvironmentVariables = false.

## Suggested fix
Treat an unusable environment proxy as absent and report it once through TurboDiagnostics.LogOnce, or at minimum move the failure to dispatch so it surfaces from the send as a normal UHttpException. Resolve and cache the environment proxy per client instead of per request.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] An unusable environment proxy is treated as absent and reported once through TurboDiagnostics.LogOnce, or the failure surfaces from the send as a UHttpException
- [ ] client.Get()/CreateRequest do not throw for an unsupported environment proxy scheme
- [ ] The environment proxy is resolved and cached per client, not per request
- [ ] Regression test under Tests/Runtime/Core/ fails before the fix and uses socks5:// and https:// values

## Context
