Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Code is as described: with Proxy null the environment is read on every CreateRequest and a non-http:// HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY throws UHttpException(InvalidRequest) (Runtime/Core/ProxySettings.cs:241-268) from ApplyDefaultMetadata, i.e. synchronously out of client.Get()/CreateRequest (Runtime/Core/UHttpClient.cs:180-190), not from the awaited send. Downgraded: the typed failure is the deliberate outcome of closed #173 (its acceptance criterion allowed 'typed UHttpException or ignored with a diagnostic'), failing closed on an unusable proxy matches curl and avoids silently going direct, and the usual 'await client.Get(url).SendBufferedAsync()' inside one try block still catches it. What remains is the throw site (builder instead of send) and the per-request environment read and NO_PROXY split; desktop players and the Editor only.

title: [Proxy] Credentials in a proxy environment variable URL are ignored and remain in ProxySettings.Address
body:
## Summary
The environment proxy is built from the URI without reading UserInfo, so Credentials stays null and a 407 is never answered. The password stays inside the proxy Uri stored in request metadata, where a logger printing metadata or the address can expose it. HTTP_PROXY=http://user:pass@proxy:3128 therefore fails every request with 407 and no hint.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/ProxySettings.cs:270`

## Problem
Resolve builds the environment proxy as new ProxySettings { Address = proxyUri, BypassList = ..., ... } (ProxySettings.cs:270-276) and never reads proxyUri.UserInfo; Credentials stays null and AllowPlaintextProxyAuth false. The transport answers a 407 only from proxy.Credentials (RawSocketTransport.cs:886, 1476) and no code in Runtime reads UserInfo for a proxy. The Uri with the userinfo is then stored in request metadata.

**Failure scenario.** HTTP_PROXY=http://user:pass@proxy:3128 (the form curl, wget and most runtimes accept): every proxied request ends in 407 with no hint that the credentials were dropped, and the password travels in request.Metadata as part of the proxy Uri, where a logger that prints metadata or the proxy address would expose it.

## Suggested fix
Either parse the userinfo into Credentials (still gated by AllowPlaintextProxyAuth, with a clear error when the gate is off) and strip it from Address, or strip it and fail with a typed message that says credentials in the proxy URL are not supported.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] UserInfo of the environment proxy URL is parsed into Credentials (subject to AllowPlaintextProxyAuth with a clear error when the gate is off), or rejected with a typed message
- [ ] UserInfo is stripped from ProxySettings.Address and request metadata
- [ ] No log, exception or metadata value contains the proxy password
- [ ] Regression test under Tests/Runtime/Core/ fails before the fix

title: [Core] RequestContext allocates unread snapshots twice per request and records timeline events and boxed state only the Editor monitor reads
body:
## Summary
The RequestContext constructor and Clear() each allocate an empty ReadOnlyDictionary over a new Dictionary, and every RecordEvent allocates a TimelineEvent and grows a List. The only reader of Timeline in Runtime is the Editor MonitorInterceptor, and boxed state values are allocated per request. Every request in a player build with no observer pays about 1 KB.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/RequestContext.cs:101`

## Problem
The constructor allocates a Stopwatch, a List<TimelineEvent>, the state Dictionary, a lock object and an eager empty ReadOnlyDictionary over a new Dictionary (96-103); Clear() allocates that empty pair again (196-197). Every RecordEvent allocates a TimelineEvent (116) and grows the list 0 -> 4 -> 8 -> 16: RawSocketTransport has 35 RecordEvent call sites and UHttpClient 10, while the only reader of Timeline in Runtime is the Editor MonitorInterceptor (MonitorInterceptor.cs:370). SetState(string, object) boxes its value: both bridges box a bool per request (BufferedDispatchBridge.cs:23, StreamingDispatchBridge.cs:23) and the transport another (RawSocketTransport.cs:154), which also forces the state dictionary's arrays to be allocated.

**Failure scenario.** Every request in a player build with no observer attached: 4 empty snapshot objects that are never read, 3 boxed bools and roughly a dozen TimelineEvent objects (about 1 KB in total) on the send path.

## Suggested fix
Share one static empty read-only snapshot for the constructor and Clear, allocate the state dictionary lazily, cache boxed true/false, and make timeline recording opt-in (set when a monitor or logging consumer is in the pipeline) or store events as structs.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The constructor and Clear() share one static empty read-only snapshot and the state dictionary is allocated lazily
- [ ] Boxed true/false state values are cached
- [ ] Timeline recording is opt-in (enabled when a monitor or logging consumer is present) or events are stored as structs
- [ ] Measured target: allocations per request from RequestContext are 0 when no observer is attached (was about 1 KB)
- [ ] Regression test under Tests/Runtime/Core/ asserts the allocation target and that the monitor still receives its timeline

title: [Core] RequestContext reads and stops its Stopwatch from different threads without synchronization
body:
## Summary
Elapsed and RecordEvent read _stopwatch.Elapsed outside the lock while Stop() and CompleteAfterResponse write it from another thread. Stopwatch is not thread-safe, and the class comment claims thread safety. On 32-bit IL2CPP a reader can see a torn 64-bit value or a double-counted interval and record a wrong timestamp.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/RequestContext.cs:165`

## Problem
Elapsed (91) and RecordEvent (116) read _stopwatch.Elapsed outside the lock while Stop() (163-167) and CompleteAfterResponse (180) write it from another thread. System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch is not thread-safe and keeps its accumulated time in a 64-bit field next to an isRunning flag. The class comment claims thread safety for concurrent access from async continuations (32).

**Failure scenario.** 32-bit IL2CPP (armv7 Android): UHttpClient's catch or finally calls context.Stop() while a transport or HTTP/2 continuation records an event or a handler reads context.Elapsed: the reader can see a torn 64-bit value, or the elapsed time counted twice between the two field writes, and stores a wrong timestamp in the timeline or metrics.

## Suggested fix
Replace the Stopwatch with a start timestamp (Stopwatch.GetTimestamp) and a stop timestamp written with Interlocked/Volatile, and compute Elapsed from those.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Elapsed is computed from a start timestamp (Stopwatch.GetTimestamp) and a stop timestamp written with Interlocked/Volatile; no shared Stopwatch is used
- [ ] Concurrent Stop() and RecordEvent/Elapsed never yield a decreasing or torn value
- [ ] Regression test under Tests/Runtime/Core/ hammers Stop and Elapsed concurrently and asserts monotonic, bounded values
- [ ] The change is exercised on a 32-bit IL2CPP device and the result is recorded (validated on a device and recorded)

title: [Core] ResponseBodyStream.Read blocks on the async read without offloading or a SynchronizationContext guard
body:
## Summary
Read() calls ReadCoreAsync(...).GetAwaiter().GetResult() with CancellationToken.None on the caller's thread and context. DecompressionHandler's equivalent bridge offloads when a SynchronizationContext is present, but this one does not, and there is no Read(Span<byte>) override. Main-thread code that passes response.Body to a synchronous consumer blocks the Unity main thread, and a source wrapper that awaits without ConfigureAwait(false) can deadlock it.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/ResponseBodyStream.cs:62`

## Problem
Read (58-65) blocks on ReadCoreAsync(...).GetAwaiter().GetResult() with CancellationToken.None; it is baselined as a synchronous Stream.Read bridge (Tools~/ci/analyzer-baseline.txt, #181). The baseline note says the equivalent bridge in DecompressionHandler offloads when a SynchronizationContext is present (DecompressionHandler.cs:463, 553-575); this one starts the source's ReadAsync on the caller's thread with the caller's context current and has no such guard. There is no Read(Span<byte>) override, so span reads go through the base class's rent-and-copy.

**Failure scenario.** Main-thread code hands response.Body to a synchronous consumer (StreamReader.ReadToEnd, a zip, XML or image parser): each Read blocks the Unity main thread until network data arrives, with no caller cancellation; if any IResponseBodySource wrapper in the chain (a third-party interceptor's body wrapper) awaits without ConfigureAwait(false), its continuation is posted to the blocked UnitySynchronizationContext and the main thread deadlocks.

## Suggested fix
When SynchronizationContext.Current is not null, run the read through Task.Run before blocking, document that synchronous reads belong on worker threads, and add a Read(Span<byte>) override.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] When SynchronizationContext.Current is not null, Read runs the underlying read off the context before blocking
- [ ] A Read(Span<byte>) override is added and documented that synchronous reads belong on worker threads
- [ ] Reading the body synchronously from a thread with a single-threaded SynchronizationContext does not deadlock
- [ ] Regression test under Tests/Runtime/Core/ fails before the fix using a source that posts continuations to a blocked context

title: [Core] Option and response APIs are inconsistent in time units, option placement and shape
body:
## Summary
Durations use int milliseconds, int seconds (Http2StallTimeoutSeconds) and TimeSpan across option types, and HTTP/2 settings are split between Http2Options and StreamingOptions. The buffered and streaming response types have different status, header and EnsureSuccess surfaces, and the send entry points return different task types. These shapes are frozen once 1.0 ships.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/StreamingOptions.cs:75`

## Problem
Time values use three conventions: int milliseconds (ConnectionPoolOptions.DnsTimeoutMs, ConnectionPoolOptions.cs:104; StreamingOptions.ExpectContinueTimeoutMs, StreamingOptions.cs:85), int seconds (StreamingOptions.Http2StallTimeoutSeconds, :75) and TimeSpan (ConnectTimeout, PingInterval, DefaultTimeout). HTTP/2 settings are split between Http2Options and StreamingOptions (DefaultHttp2PerStreamReceiveBufferBytes :52, Http2StallTimeoutSeconds :75, MaxConnectionBufferedBytes :64), and the HTTP/2 default constant lives on UHttpClientOptions (UHttpClientOptions.cs:14). UHttpRequest.SendBufferedAsync returns ValueTask<UHttpResponse> (UHttpRequest.cs:373) while UHttpClient.SendBufferedAsync returns Task<UHttpResponse> (UHttpClient.cs:377). UHttpStreamingResponse has no IsSuccessStatusCode, EnsureSuccessStatusCode, Request or ElapsedTime (UHttpStreamingResponse.cs:9-35) although UHttpResponse has all four, and the two share no base type. UHttpClientOptions, UHttpResponse, HttpHeaders, RequestContext and UHttpError are unsealed while their siblings are sealed; UHttpClientOptions.Clone is non-virtual and slices subclasses (UHttpClientOptions.cs:180).

**Failure scenario.** Callers set Http2StallTimeoutSeconds = 60000 expecting milliseconds; code written against UHttpResponse (response.EnsureSuccessStatusCode()) does not port to the streaming path; these shapes are frozen once 1.0 ships.

## Suggested fix
Before GA: use TimeSpan for all durations, keep HTTP/2 knobs in Http2Options, give both response types a common status/headers/EnsureSuccess surface, pick Task or ValueTask for both send entry points, and seal the option and model types.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] All duration options use TimeSpan, with the old members removed or obsoleted
- [ ] HTTP/2 knobs live in Http2Options only
- [ ] Buffered and streaming response types share a common status/headers/EnsureSuccess surface and the send entry points use one task type
- [ ] Option and model types are sealed where intended and the API baseline is updated
- [ ] Regression test under Tests/Runtime/Core/ covers the renamed options and the shared response surface

title: [Core] UHttpClient options validation is inconsistent: the only constructor check is unreachable, BaseUrl, Proxy and PluginShutdownTimeout are not validated up front
body:
## Summary
The Http2.MaxDecodedHeaderBytes check in the constructor cannot run because the setter already rejects the value. BaseUrl is parsed on every CreateRequest and a bad value throws a raw UriFormatException from Get(), Proxy is validated per request, and a negative PluginShutdownTimeout silently prevents plugin shutdown on dispose. Misconfiguration surfaces far from where it was made.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/UHttpClient.cs:103`

## Problem
UHttpClient.cs:103-109 throws when Http2.MaxDecodedHeaderBytes <= 0, but the setter already rejects that (Http2Options.cs:126) and Clone copies the field, so the branch cannot run. BaseUrl is parsed on every CreateRequest (new Uri(...), UHttpClient.cs:743) and a bad value throws UriFormatException from Get(). options.Proxy is validated on every CreateRequest (ProxySettings.cs:232) and an https:// address throws ArgumentException from Get(). A negative PluginShutdownTimeout makes new CancellationTokenSource(timeout) throw inside the try at UHttpClient.cs:652, which is logged as 'Plugin dispose failed' and the plugin's ShutdownAsync is never called. Http2Options.InitialWindowSize tests value > int.MaxValue (Http2Options.cs:80), which is always false.

**Failure scenario.** new UHttpClient(new UHttpClientOptions { BaseUrl = 'api.example.com' }) succeeds; the first client.Get('users') throws a raw UriFormatException far from the misconfiguration. With PluginShutdownTimeout = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(-5) plugins are never shut down on dispose.

## Suggested fix
Validate the whole snapshot once in the constructor (BaseUrl absolute http/https and cached as a Uri, Proxy.Validate(), timeouts in range) and remove the dead checks.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The constructor validates the whole options snapshot once: BaseUrl is an absolute http/https URI cached as a Uri, Proxy.Validate() passes, timeouts are in range
- [ ] Invalid options throw a typed exception from the constructor
- [ ] The dead MaxDecodedHeaderBytes check is removed

title: [Core] UHttpClient constructor leaks an owned transport and its idle-scavenger task when pipeline composition throws
body:
## Summary
Only InterceptorOrdering.FindViolation runs before the transport is created, and it tolerates null entries. TcpConnectionPool starts an idle scavenger task in its constructor, and new InterceptorPipeline(...) then throws ArgumentException for a null element, leaving the transport running for the life of the process. Repeated in a retry loop it accumulates.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/UHttpClient.cs:143`

## Problem
The comment at UHttpClient.cs:111 says a rejected configuration leaks nothing, but only InterceptorOrdering.FindViolation runs before the transport is created; it tolerates null entries (InterceptorOrdering.GetRole on null returns None). CreateWithOptions runs at :130-134 and TcpConnectionPool's constructor starts Task.Run(RunIdleScavengerAsync) (Runtime/Transport/Tcp/TcpConnectionPool.cs:375). new InterceptorPipeline(...) at :143 then throws ArgumentException for a null element (Pipeline/InterceptorPipeline.cs:30-31) or propagates an exception from IHttpInterceptor.Wrap (:34); nothing disposes _transport. InterceptorPipeline also does not check for a null DispatchFunc returned by Wrap.

**Failure scenario.** new UHttpClient(new UHttpClientOptions { Http2 = { MaxConcurrentStreams = 50 }, Interceptors = { null } }) throws ArgumentException and leaves a transport whose scavenger loop runs for the life of the process; repeated in a retry loop it accumulates.

## Suggested fix
Build and validate the pipeline against a placeholder before creating the transport, or wrap the tail of the constructor in try/catch that disposes an owned transport; reject null entries and null Wrap results up front.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Constructor failure after the owned transport is created disposes that transport
- [ ] Null interceptor entries and null Wrap results are rejected before the transport is created
- [ ] Regression test under Tests/Runtime/Core/ fails before the fix: constructing with a null interceptor leaves no running scavenger or undisposed transport

title: [Core] RegisterPluginAsync holds the lifecycle gate during InitializeAsync and wraps cancellation in PluginException
body:
## Summary
UHttpClient.RegisterPluginAsync takes a non-reentrant SemaphoreSlim and holds it while the plugin's InitializeAsync runs. A plugin that registers a dependency from its own InitializeAsync therefore waits forever on the gate its caller holds. The catch block also converts the caller's OperationCanceledException into PluginException, which breaks the library's cancellation contract.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/UHttpClient.cs:246`

## Problem
The non-reentrant SemaphoreSlim _pluginLifecycleGate is taken at UHttpClient.cs:222 and held while plugin.InitializeAsync runs (:246); RegisterPluginAsync and UnregisterPluginAsync both wait on it (:222, :308). The catch at :252-259 wraps every exception, including the OperationCanceledException of the caller's own token, in PluginException('failed during initialization').

**Failure scenario.** A composite plugin registers a dependency from its InitializeAsync (await client.RegisterPluginAsync(dep)): the inner call waits forever on the gate its caller holds. A caller that cancels registration gets PluginException instead of OperationCanceledException, against the library's cancellation contract.

## Suggested fix
Rethrow OperationCanceledException when ct is cancelled, and either detect re-entrant registration (AsyncLocal or a 'registering' flag that throws InvalidOperationException) or document that the gate is held.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] When the caller's CancellationToken is cancelled during plugin initialization, RegisterPluginAsync throws OperationCanceledException, not PluginException
- [ ] A plugin that calls RegisterPluginAsync from its own InitializeAsync fails fast with InvalidOperationException (or is supported), and never deadlocks
- [ ] The behaviour of the lifecycle gate is documented on RegisterPluginAsync

body:

As #182; when splitting, extract one shared send prologue/epilogue and one completion helper generic over the collector.

title: [Core] A send racing UHttpClient.Dispose skips every interceptor via the raw transport instead of throwing ObjectDisposedException
body:
## Summary
SendBufferedAsync and SendStreamingAsync read '_pipeline ?? _transport.DispatchAsync' after ThrowIfDisposed. After Dispose the pipeline is null, so with the shared default transport the request is dispatched with no auth, cookie, redirect, cache or policy interceptor. The window is small but real on scene unload.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/UHttpClient.cs:401`

## Problem
SendBufferedAsync and SendStreamingAsync check ThrowIfDisposed (UHttpClient.cs:384, :453) and later read 'var pipelineSnapshot = _pipeline ?? _transport.DispatchAsync' (:401, :471). _pipeline is assigned in the constructor (:143) and is only ever null after BeginDispose (:584) or RebuildPipelineSnapshot_NoLock on a disposed client (:696-700), so the fallback exists solely for the disposed case. With the shared default transport (_ownsTransport false, :139-140) the transport stays alive. Tests/Runtime/Core/UHttpClientDisposeRaceTests.cs covers plugin registration races only.

**Failure scenario.** Thread A passes ThrowIfDisposed; thread B calls Dispose (scene unload); thread A reads _pipeline == null and dispatches straight to the shared default transport: no auth, cookie, redirect, cache, concurrency-limit or user policy interceptor runs, and the request is still sent. With an owned transport the caller gets UHttpException(Unknown) wrapping ObjectDisposedException.

## Suggested fix
Read _pipeline once and throw ObjectDisposedException when it is null; remove the transport fallback.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A send that observes a disposed client throws ObjectDisposedException and never dispatches to the transport
- [ ] The transport fallback for a null pipeline is removed; _pipeline is read once per send
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Core/ that fails before the fix and passes after it (dispose between ThrowIfDisposed and the pipeline read, asserting no transport dispatch)

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `core-design-06` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/core.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: best-practices.

With the shared default transport (_ownsTransport false, :139-140) the request is then dispatched with no interceptor. No lock or re-check covers the window; UHttpClientDisposeRaceTests covers plugin registration only. title: [Core] Plugin-contributed interceptors are always appended innermost; RegisterInterceptor has no placement argument
body:
## Summary
BuildCombinedInterceptors_NoLock appends base interceptors then plugin contributions in registration order, and PluginContext.RegisterInterceptor takes no position. A client configured with CacheInterceptor can never accept a plugin that contributes an AuthInterceptor, and role-less third-party interceptors are placed in a hazardous position silently.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/UHttpClient.cs:705`

## Problem
BuildCombinedInterceptors_NoLock appends base interceptors, then each plugin's contributions in registration order (UHttpClient.cs:705-717); PluginContext.RegisterInterceptor has no position argument (PluginContext.cs:45). The combined list is then validated (UHttpClient.cs:268-269). Tests/Runtime/Core/InterceptorOrderTests.cs PluginContributingAuthInsideBaseCache_IsRejectedAndShutDown asserts the rejection.

title: [Core] ResolveUri turns a leading-slash relative URL into file:///path on Unix runtimes, ignoring BaseUrl
body:
## Summary
UHttpClient.ResolveUri calls Uri.TryCreate(url, UriKind.Absolute) first and returns on success. On Mono and .NET for Unix a string starting with '/' parses as an implicit file path, so BaseUrl is never used and the transport later fails with 'Unsupported URI scheme: file'. The documented BaseUrl pattern in the README and QuickStart therefore works on Windows but fails on macOS, Linux, iOS and Android.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/UHttpClient.cs:733`

## Problem
ResolveUri (UHttpClient.cs:731-745) first calls Uri.TryCreate(url, UriKind.Absolute, ...) and returns the result when it succeeds; BaseUrl is only used otherwise. On Mono and .NET for Unix a string starting with '/' is an implicit absolute file path, so TryCreate succeeds with scheme 'file' (the reason Mono has the DotNetRelativeOrAbsolute UriKind workaround). Nothing in Core rejects non-http schemes; the transport later throws 'Unsupported URI scheme: file' (Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:451-458). README.md:111, Documentation~/QuickStart.md:162, Documentation~/Modules/Core.md:55 and Samples~/02, 04, 05 all use client.Get('/...') with BaseUrl. The only resolution test uses 'users' without a slash (Tests/Runtime/Core/UHttpClientTests.Builders.cs:90-95); UHttpRequestBuilderJsonTests.cs:38 uses '/api' but never checks the URI.

**Failure scenario.** BaseUrl = 'https://api.example.com'; client.Get('/data').SendBufferedAsync() works in the Windows Editor and fails on an Android, iOS, macOS or Linux player with UHttpException(InvalidRequest, 'Unsupported URI scheme: file'). Confirm by asserting client.Get('/x').Uri on a macOS Editor or an Android player.

## Suggested fix
When BaseUrl is set, resolve against it unless the parsed absolute URI has an http or https scheme (or check for '://' before trying absolute). Reject other schemes in CreateRequest with InvalidRequest. Add a test for '/path' that asserts the resolved URI and runs on a non-Windows runner.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] With BaseUrl set, Get("/data") resolves to BaseUrl + "/data" on every platform, including query strings
- [ ] An absolute URL is used as given only when its scheme is http or https; other schemes are rejected in CreateRequest with UHttpException(InvalidRequest)
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Core/ that fails before the fix and passes after it asserting the resolved Uri for '/path' and '/path?x=1'; it must run on a non-Windows runner
- [ ] Behaviour validated on an Android or iOS player and recorded

## Context

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: ResolveUri returns the Uri.TryCreate(url, UriKind.Absolute) result with no scheme check (Runtime/Core/UHttpClient.cs:731-734); BaseUrl is only reached when that fails. I ran Uri.TryCreate("/data", UriKind.Absolute) on .NET 8 on Linux in the scratchpad: it returns true with file:///data ("/api/users?x=1" becomes file:///api/users%3Fx=1). Nothing in Core rejects the scheme; the transport throws InvalidRequest 'Unsupported URI scheme' (Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:451-458). The pattern is documented and sampled: README.md:111, Documentation~/QuickStart.md:162, Documentation~/Modules/Core.md:55/121, Samples~/02, 04, 05. Tests only resolve "users" (Tests/Runtime/Core/UHttpClientTests.Builders.cs:90-95); UHttpRequestBuilderJsonTests.cs:38 uses "/api" but never asserts the URI. Not executed on Unity: Mono/IL2CPP on macOS, Linux, iOS and Android apply the same implicit-Unix-file-path rule for UriKind.Absolute (the reason Mono has DotNetRelativeOrAbsolute), so the same failure is expected there, but it needs one device/Mac Editor assertion (needs-device-validation). Windows Editor resolves against BaseUrl, which explains why it went unnoticed. No issue tracks it.

title: [Core] Client policy (cleartext, proxy, default headers, timeout) is applied only in CreateRequest; standalone requests skip it
body:
## Summary
ApplyDefaultMetadata and ApplyDefaultHeaders run only from UHttpClient.CreateRequest. A request built with the public UHttpRequest constructor, or one whose metadata was replaced with WithMetadata, is sent with no client policy: cleartext allowed by desktop defaults, direct instead of through the configured proxy, no default headers and a hard-coded 30 s timeout. A client configured with AllowCleartext = false and a corporate proxy can thus leak requests.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/UHttpClient.cs:747`

## Problem
UHttpClient.ApplyDefaultMetadata (UHttpClient.cs:747-760) and ApplyDefaultHeaders (:182) run only from CreateRequest (:169-191). SendBufferedAsync/SendStreamingAsync (:377, :446) accept any UHttpRequest and apply nothing. The public constructor (UHttpRequest.cs:115-131) starts with empty metadata and a hard-coded 30 s timeout (UHttpRequest.cs:147) while the client default is PlatformConfig.RecommendedTimeout (45 s on mobile, UHttpClientOptions.cs:40). WithMetadata(IReadOnlyDictionary) (UHttpRequest.cs:354-367) clears every key, including the ones the client wrote. The transport then falls back to platform defaults: ResolveAllowCleartext returns CleartextTrafficPolicy.DefaultAllowCleartext when the key is absent and ResolveProxySettings returns null (Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:1298-1327). No test in Tests/Runtime/Core sends a standalone request through a client with non-default options.

**Failure scenario.** Desktop app: new UHttpClient(new UHttpClientOptions { AllowCleartext = false, Proxy = corporateProxy, DefaultHeaders = { apiKey } }); client.SendBufferedAsync(new UHttpRequest(HttpMethod.GET, new Uri('http://host/x'))) goes out in cleartext (desktop default is true), directly instead of through the proxy, without the default headers, with a 30 s timeout. The same happens to a client-created request after request.WithMetadata(myDictionary).

## Suggested fix
Apply client policy at send time inside UHttpClient (resolve effective cleartext/proxy/redirect settings from _options when the request does not override them, and merge default headers for requests the client did not create), or reject requests that were not created by the client. Keep per-request overrides as explicit typed fields rather than replaceable string keys.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Effective cleartext, proxy, redirect and timeout settings are resolved from the client options at send time for any request that does not override them
- [ ] Default headers are merged for requests the client did not create
- [ ] A request with AllowCleartext = false client option and an http:// URI is rejected whether built via CreateRequest or the public constructor
- [ ] WithMetadata(dictionary) does not remove client policy
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Core/ that fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. ApplyDefaultHeaders/ApplyDefaultMetadata run only in CreateRequest (Runtime/Core/UHttpClient.cs:179-183, 747-760). SendBufferedAsync/SendStreamingAsync accept a standalone request (only a foreign client-owned request is rejected, :386, :455) and apply nothing; UHttpRequest.cs:376-378 even tells callers to use client.SendBufferedAsync(request) for standalone requests, and Tests/Runtime/Core/UHttpClientTests.Execution.cs:34 does so. Public ctor: empty metadata, 30 s timeout (UHttpRequest.cs:147-150). WithMetadata(dictionary) clears every key (UHttpRequest.cs:360). Fallbacks: ResolveAllowCleartext returns CleartextTrafficPolicy.DefaultAllowCleartext when the key is absent (Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:1298-1308; true in Editor/desktop, CleartextTrafficPolicy.cs:29-33), ResolveProxySettings returns null (:1310-1326), and RedirectInterceptor falls back to its own default (true) when FollowRedirects is absent (Runtime/Middleware/RedirectInterceptor.cs:24, 265-272), so a client-level FollowRedirects=false is lost too. Limits: on iOS/Android players the absent key fails closed for cleartext; docs and samples only use the client builders and WithMetadata(key, value); RequestMetadataKeys.cs:19-23 documents the absent-key fallback. title: [Core] CreateRequest re-reads proxy environment variables and re-parses proxy rules for every request
body:
## Summary
ApplyDefaultMetadata boxes FollowRedirects, MaxRedirects and AllowCleartext on each call and calls ProxyEnvironmentResolver.Resolve, which reads proxy environment variables, re-parses the proxy Uri and NO_PROXY and allocates a ProxySettings every time. On mobile each request makes native getenv round trips for values that do not change during the client's life.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/UHttpClient.cs:756`

## Problem
ApplyDefaultMetadata (747-760) boxes FollowRedirects, MaxRedirects and AllowCleartext per request (749-751) and calls ProxyEnvironmentResolver.Resolve (756). With the default Proxy == null that reads HTTPS_PROXY/https_proxy or HTTP_PROXY/http_proxy through Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable on every CreateRequest (ProxySettings.cs:244-247, 281-303) and, when a variable is set, re-parses the proxy Uri, re-reads and re-splits NO_PROXY into a new List and allocates a new ProxySettings (251-278). With a configured proxy it re-validates and re-runs bypass matching with Trim/Substring per rule (232-239, 87-152).

**Failure scenario.** On a desktop or CI machine with HTTPS_PROXY and NO_PROXY set, each request repeats 3-4 environment reads, a Uri parse, a Split and a rule match with ten or more allocations; on mobile each request still makes two native getenv round trips and three boxes for values that never change during the client's life.

## Suggested fix
Resolve environment proxy settings once per client (or cache them keyed by the raw variable strings), precompile bypass rules, and keep the three boxed metadata values in the client.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Environment proxy settings are resolved once per client (or cached keyed by the raw variable strings) and bypass rules are precompiled
- [ ] The three boxed metadata values are held by the client and reused
- [ ] CreateRequest with no proxy configured performs no environment reads and no proxy allocations per call (assert with an allocation measurement or a counting resolver)

title: [Core] Editor monitor auto-wiring reads Application.isPlaying off the main thread and skips clients built on pool threads
body:
## Summary
TryAppendEditorMonitorInterceptor reads UnityEngine.Application.isPlaying on whichever thread constructs the client. That API is main-thread-only and throws on a thread-pool thread, and the exception is swallowed as 'not playing'. Clients created in Task.Run or after ConfigureAwait(false) never appear in the HTTP Monitor.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/UHttpClient.cs:810`

## Problem
TryAppendEditorMonitorInterceptor (802-823) calls UnityEngine.Application.isPlaying (829) on whatever thread constructs the client and treats any exception as not playing (808-815). Application.isPlaying is a main-thread-only Unity API (unlike Application.platform), so it throws UnityException from a thread-pool thread.

**Failure scenario.** Editor Play Mode: a UHttpClient created inside Task.Run or after ConfigureAwait(false) gets no monitor interceptor, so its requests never appear in the HTTP Monitor, and each such construction throws and catches a UnityException; the same code on the main thread is monitored.

## Suggested fix
Capture the play-mode state on the main thread into a volatile static (RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod plus EditorApplication.playModeStateChanged, reset at SubsystemRegistration) and read that flag in the constructor. Confirm the thread affinity in the Editor.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The play-mode state is captured on the main thread into a volatile static and read from the constructor; no exception is thrown or caught per construction
- [ ] A client created from a thread-pool thread in Play Mode is monitored
- [ ] Thread affinity of Application.isPlaying confirmed in the Editor and recorded

title: [Core] FollowRedirects and MaxRedirects live in Core but only Middleware honours them; default client contradicts its defaults
body:
## Summary
FollowRedirects defaults to true and MaxRedirects to 10 in UHttpClientOptions, but only TurboHTTP.Middleware.RedirectInterceptor reads them. A default new UHttpClient() returns 3xx responses to the caller, logs a warning on first construction when Middleware is not used, and boxes two metadata entries per request for a feature that may not be installed.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/UHttpClientOptions.cs:98`

## Problem
FollowRedirects defaults to true (UHttpClientOptions.cs:98) and MaxRedirects to 10 (:104). Core only copies them into each request's metadata as boxed values (UHttpClient.cs:749-750); TurboHTTP.Middleware.RedirectInterceptor reads them (Runtime/Middleware/RedirectInterceptor.cs:264-290) and already has its own constructor defaults. Without that interceptor the client logs a one-time warning (UHttpClient.cs:146-161, #64). No assembly adds the interceptor by default.

**Failure scenario.** new UHttpClient() with default options returns 3xx responses to the caller although FollowRedirects is true, and writes a warning on first construction in every project that does not use the Middleware module; every request pays two boxed metadata entries for a feature that may not be installed.

## Suggested fix
Move the two settings to RedirectInterceptor/RedirectOptions (keeping per-request overrides as Middleware extension methods), or default FollowRedirects to false in Core and let the Middleware module set it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The redirect settings move to RedirectInterceptor/RedirectOptions with per-request overrides as Middleware extension methods, or FollowRedirects defaults to false in Core and Middleware enables it
- [ ] A default-constructed client with no Middleware logs no redirect warning and its documented defaults match its behaviour

title: [Core] UHttpException.ToString drops the stack trace and the inner exception
body:
## Summary
UHttpException overrides ToString to return only 'UHttpException: ' plus the structured error line. Debug.LogError(ex) and crash reporters that use ToString therefore lose the stack and the inner SocketException or AuthenticationException, which usually hold the cause.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/UHttpError.cs:118`

## Problem
UHttpException overrides ToString to return 'UHttpException: ' + HttpError (UHttpError.cs:118-121); UHttpError.ToString prints type, status and message only (:94-98). Exception.ToString normally includes the stack trace and the inner exception chain.

**Failure scenario.** Debug.LogError(ex) or a crash reporter that records ex.ToString() shows one line such as 'UHttpException: [Unknown] Specified argument was out of the range of valid values' with no stack and no inner SocketException/AuthenticationException, which is where the cause is.

## Suggested fix
Remove the override, or prepend the structured line and then append base.ToString().

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] UHttpException.ToString includes the structured error line followed by base.ToString() (stack trace and inner exception chain), or the override is removed
- [ ] The output still redacts nothing less than today (no new sensitive data in the message)

title: [Core] UHttpRequest.Clone and CopyWithSharedContent deep-clone headers and metadata twice
body:
## Summary
Clone() and CopyWithSharedContent() pass already cloned headers and a copied metadata dictionary to a private constructor that clones both again. CopyWithSharedContent is the per-request rewrite primitive of the Auth, Cookie, Decompression, DefaultHeaders, Adaptive and Cache interceptors, so a request with 10 headers through three interceptors allocates about 120 list/array objects and 6 metadata dictionaries, half of them discarded immediately.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/UHttpRequest.cs:144`

## Problem
Clone() (159-170) and CopyWithSharedContent() (514-526) pass _headers.Clone() and new Dictionary<string, object>(_metadata) to the private constructor, which clones both again: _headers = headers?.Clone() (144) and new Dictionary<string, object>(metadata) (148-150). HttpHeaders.Clone allocates a Dictionary plus one List<string> and its array per header (HttpHeaders.cs:127-135). CopyWithSharedContent is the per-request rewrite primitive of DefaultHeadersInterceptor.cs:46, CookieInterceptor.cs:67, DecompressionInterceptor.cs:70, AuthInterceptor.cs:73, AdaptiveInterceptor.cs:60, CacheInterceptor.cs:435 and RawSocketTransport.cs:410/538/1351/1363.

**Failure scenario.** A request with 10 headers through Auth + Cookie + Decompression: 3 copies x 2 clones = 6 header dictionaries, about 120 List/array objects and 6 metadata dictionaries per request, half of them created and dropped inside the constructor call.

## Suggested fix
Add an internal constructor path that takes ownership of an already cloned HttpHeaders and metadata dictionary for Clone and CopyWithSharedContent; keep the defensive clone on the public constructor and CreateDerived only.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Clone and CopyWithSharedContent clone headers and metadata exactly once, via an internal constructor that takes ownership; the public constructor and CreateDerived keep their defensive clone
- [ ] Allocation target: CopyWithSharedContent on a 10-header request allocates one HttpHeaders clone and one metadata dictionary (half of the current count), shown by an allocation test or benchmark

title: [Core] Request timeouts are not validated at public entry points; CancelAfter-rejected values fail every request as Unknown
body:
## Summary
WithTimeout, the UHttpRequest constructor and UHttpClientOptions.DefaultTimeout accept any TimeSpan, but the transport calls CancelAfter(request.Timeout), which throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException for values above int.MaxValue ms or below -1 ms. The exception is mapped to UHttpException(Unknown) with a message that does not name the timeout, so options.DefaultTimeout = TimeSpan.MaxValue makes every request fail.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/UHttpRequest.cs:330`

## Problem
UHttpRequest.WithTimeout (UHttpRequest.cs:330-336), the public constructor (:147) and UHttpClientOptions.DefaultTimeout (UHttpClientOptions.cs:40) accept any TimeSpan. The transport calls timeoutCts.CancelAfter(request.Timeout) (Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:440), which on .NET Standard 2.1 throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException for values below -1 ms or above int.MaxValue ms. DispatchAsync only catches UHttpException and OperationCanceledException (RawSocketTransport.cs:176-187), so the bridge converts the fault to UHttpException(Unknown, 'Specified argument was out of the range of valid values') (ResponseCollectorHandler.cs:107-109). Other options in the same family validate in their setters (ConnectionPoolOptions.ConnectTimeout, ConnectionPoolOptions.cs:127-144).

**Failure scenario.** options.DefaultTimeout = TimeSpan.MaxValue (a common spelling of 'no timeout') or request.WithTimeout(TimeSpan.FromDays(30)): every request fails immediately with UHttpErrorType.Unknown and a message that does not name the timeout.

## Suggested fix
Validate in WithTimeout, the constructor and the DefaultTimeout setter: positive and at most int.MaxValue ms, or Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan; throw ArgumentOutOfRangeException there (the pattern ConnectTimeout already uses).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] WithTimeout, the constructor and the DefaultTimeout setter accept only positive values up to int.MaxValue ms or Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan and otherwise throw ArgumentOutOfRangeException naming the parameter
- [ ] TimeSpan.MaxValue and TimeSpan.FromDays(30) are rejected at the entry point, not at send time
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Core/ that fails before the fix and passes after it

Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `core-design-07` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/core.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: best-practices.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. No validation in WithTimeout (Runtime/Core/UHttpRequest.cs:330-336), the public ctor (:147), UHttpClientOptions.DefaultTimeout (UHttpClientOptions.cs:40) or the UHttpClient ctor (only Http2.MaxDecodedHeaderBytes is checked, UHttpClient.cs:103-109). The transport calls timeoutCts.CancelAfter(request.Timeout) (Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:440); DispatchAsync catches only UHttpException and OperationCanceledException (:176-187), so the ArgumentOutOfRangeException reaches the bridge and becomes UHttpException(Unknown) (Runtime/Core/Pipeline/ResponseCollectorHandler.cs:107-109). I ran CancelAfter(TimeSpan.MaxValue) on .NET 8: ArgumentOutOfRangeException. 30 days is accepted on .NET 8 (limit about 49.7 days) but exceeds the int.MaxValue ms limit of the .NET Standard 2.1 / Mono implementation, so that part is runtime-dependent. Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan works. Downgraded: a misconfiguration that fails every request at once and deterministically, with the original exception attached; the cost is a misleading error type and message.

title: [Core] UHttpRequest.ToString and the relative-URL exception print the full URL including userinfo and query
body:
## Summary
UHttpRequest.ToString returns the method and Uri, and Uri.ToString keeps userinfo and the query. ResolveUri also embeds the caller's URL in its InvalidOperationException message. Logging a request or that exception writes passwords and API keys to device logs and crash reports, against the rule that nothing sensitive reaches logs or exceptions.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/UHttpRequest.cs:407`

## Problem
ToString returns $"{Method} {Uri}" (UHttpRequest.cs:407-410); Uri.ToString keeps userinfo and the query (a scratch run printed 'https://user:secret@example.com/p?token=abc'). ResolveUri embeds the caller's URL in its InvalidOperationException message (UHttpClient.cs:739-740). CLAUDE.md section 3 requires that nothing sensitive reaches logs or exceptions and that redaction is on by default; the redaction policy lives in Observability (RedactionPolicy.cs:172-183) and is not applied here. #117 plans one RedactionPolicy for exceptions and timelines but does not list these two sites.

**Failure scenario.** Application code logs a request (Debug.Log($"sending {request}")) or logs the exception from client.Get("items?api_key=...") without a BaseUrl: the password in the userinfo or the key in the query string is written to the device log or a crash report.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 Section 4.2.4

## Suggested fix
Print scheme, host, port and path only in ToString (drop userinfo, redact or drop the query), and do not echo the URL in the ResolveUri message.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] UHttpRequest.ToString prints scheme, host, port and path only; userinfo is dropped and the query is dropped or redacted
- [ ] The ResolveUri exception message does not include the caller's URL

title: [Core] UHttpRequest.BeginSend and Dispose are check-then-act; a send can start on a lease Dispose just completed
body:
## Summary
BeginSend checks disposed state and then CASes _sendInProgress; Dispose sets _disposeRequested and completes the lease when it reads _sendInProgress == 0. Neither side re-checks after its own write, so both can succeed: the send proceeds on a dead lease, content is nulled, and the failure surfaces later as UHttpException(Unknown) after a context, collector and possibly a connection were set up.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/UHttpRequest.cs:441`

## Problem
BeginSend (439-455) calls ThrowIfDisposed, checks _responseHoldCount and then CASes _sendInProgress. Dispose (428-431) sets _disposeRequested and TryCompleteLease (547-562) completes the lease when it reads _sendInProgress == 0. Neither side re-checks after its own write, so both can succeed.

**Failure scenario.** Thread A is inside BeginSend past ThrowIfDisposed; thread B calls request.Dispose(): the lease completes and DisposeContent sets _content to null (728-737); A's CAS succeeds and the send proceeds on a dead lease. The first request.Content access in the transport throws ObjectDisposedException, which surfaces as UHttpException(Unknown) after a RequestContext, a collector and possibly a connection were set up.

## Suggested fix
After the _sendInProgress CAS re-check _disposeRequested and _isLeased; when set, reset the flag, call TryCompleteLease and throw ObjectDisposedException.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] After the _sendInProgress CAS, BeginSend re-checks _disposeRequested and _isLeased; if set it resets the flag, completes the lease and throws ObjectDisposedException
- [ ] A concurrent BeginSend/Dispose never results in a send on a completed lease
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Core/ that fails before the fix and passes after it using a deterministic interleaving (no wall-clock sleeps)

title: [Core] Request header validation covers only CR/LF in WithHeader; Headers.Set/Add, WithHeaders and the constructor validate nothing
body:
## Summary
UHttpRequest.WithHeader rejects CR and LF only, while NUL, other control characters, DEL, non-Latin-1 characters and non-token names pass. request.Headers is a live mutable collection, and WithHeaders, the public constructor, WithExpectContinue and the default headers skip validation. Invalid headers therefore fail only at dispatch, far from the call site, and custom transports or interceptors can see them.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/UHttpRequest.cs:577`

## Problem
ValidateHeaderInput (UHttpRequest.cs:577-583) checks CR and LF only: NUL, other C0 controls, DEL, non-Latin-1 characters and non-token names ('X Y', 'Foo:', ':path') pass. HttpHeaders.Set/Add accept any non-blank name and any value (HttpHeaders.cs:35-64), and request.Headers is the live mutable collection (UHttpRequest.cs:47), so request.Headers.Set("X", "a\r\nEvil: 1") bypasses even the CR/LF check; so do WithHeaders (192-202), the public constructor (144), WithExpectContinue and UHttpClientOptions.DefaultHeaders via CopyHeaders (585-600). The raw-socket transport catches all of this at serialization (Runtime/Transport/Internal/HttpFieldValidator.cs:28-107, called from Http11RequestSerializer.cs:518 and Http2Connection.Send.cs:457), so nothing reaches that wire. The only Core test is WithHeader with CR/LF (Tests/Runtime/Core/CoreTypesTests.cs:267-278).

**Failure scenario.** A header built from user input with an embedded NUL or newline is accepted by the request API and fails only at dispatch, as a transport error far from the call site. Any other consumer of the request (a custom IHttpTransport, MockTransport, RecordReplayTransport, a logging or signing interceptor that writes headers out) receives the unvalidated name and value with no protection of its own.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 Sections 5.1 and 5.5

## Suggested fix
Move the RFC 9110 token and field-value checks into Core (HttpHeaders.Set/Add for request headers, or one shared validator used by WithHeader, WithHeaders, the constructor and DefaultHeaders) and keep the transport check as the last line; cover NUL and invalid names in the Core tests.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Request header names must be RFC 9110 tokens and values must contain no NUL, CR, LF or other disallowed control characters, enforced for WithHeader, WithHeaders, the constructor, Headers.Set/Add and DefaultHeaders
- [ ] Violations throw at the call site with a clear exception; the transport check stays as a last line
- [ ] Tests/Runtime/Core/: a deterministic NUnit regression test covers NUL, embedded CRLF via Headers.Set, and invalid names such as 'X Y', 'Foo:' and ':path', and fails before the fix

title: [Core] IHttpTransport is public but a third-party transport cannot read stream or factory request bodies or transport flags
body:
## Summary
IHttpTransport and UHttpClientOptions.Transport are public and documented as replaceable, but StreamRequestBody and FactoryRequestBody can be read only through the internal OpenReadSessionAsync, and UHttpRequestBody cannot be subclassed outside Core. A custom transport can send buffered bodies but not WithStreamBody or WithBodyFactory uploads, and cannot tell streaming from buffered sends.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/UHttpRequestBody.cs:100`

## Problem
IHttpTransport's summary says it 'can be replaced for testing (mock transport) or platform-specific backends' (IHttpTransport.cs:8-11) and UHttpClientOptions.Transport is public. The only way to read a StreamRequestBody or FactoryRequestBody is the internal OpenReadSessionAsync (UHttpRequestBody.cs:100); their TryGetBufferedData returns false (:434-438, :506-510) and RequestBodyReadSession is internal. The three first-party transports call it through InternalsVisibleTo (Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11RequestSerializer.cs:107, Http2/Http2Connection.Send.cs:156, RawSocketTransport.cs:2348); Runtime/Testing's mocks use the same access. TransportBehaviorFlags (streaming requested, bytes sent) is internal (Internal/TransportBehaviorFlags.cs:3-8). UHttpRequestBody is a public abstract class with protected helpers but internal abstract members (UHttpRequestBody.cs:45, :133), so no external subclass compiles. #76 lists request derivation and body discard for interceptors; the transport and body contracts are not in it.

**Failure scenario.** A customer writes a transport (platform HTTP stack, in-house test double) against the public interface: buffered bodies work, but request.WithStreamBody(file) or WithBodyFactory uploads cannot be read at all, and the transport cannot tell a streaming send from a buffered one.

## Suggested fix
Add a public read-session API on UHttpRequestBody (for example OpenReadStreamAsync returning a Stream plus length) and public constants or typed accessors for the transport flags; give UHttpRequestBody a private protected constructor so the closed hierarchy is explicit. Fold into #76.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] UHttpRequestBody exposes a public, documented way to read stream and factory bodies (for example OpenReadStreamAsync returning a Stream and length)
- [ ] Transport flags are available through public constants or typed accessors
- [ ] UHttpRequestBody has a private protected constructor so the hierarchy is explicitly closed
- [ ] Tests/Runtime/Core/: a deterministic NUnit regression test with a transport defined outside the friend assemblies sends a stream body and a factory body, and fails before the fix

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. IHttpTransport is public and its summary advertises replacement (Runtime/Core/IHttpTransport.cs:8-13). The only way to read a StreamRequestBody or FactoryRequestBody is the internal OpenReadSessionAsync / OpenReadSessionCoreAsync (Runtime/Core/UHttpRequestBody.cs:100, :133); their TryGetBufferedData returns false (:434-438, :506-510) and no public member exposes the stream or factory. UHttpRequestBody is public abstract with internal abstract members (:45, :133), so it cannot be subclassed outside the friend assemblies. TransportBehaviorFlags is internal (Runtime/Core/Internal/TransportBehaviorFlags.cs:3-8). Open #76 tracks the same InternalsVisibleTo boundary problem, but its scope and acceptance criteria name only interceptor primitives (request derivation, body discard); the transport read-session and flag contracts are not listed, so #76 understates this and needs amending.

title: [Core] OwnedMemoryRequestBody and StreamRequestBody finalizers dispose caller-supplied IMemoryOwner and Stream objects
body:
## Summary
The two body types declare finalizers that run DisposeCore, disposing the caller's IMemoryOwner<byte> or Stream on the finalizer thread. This violates the rule that a finalizer never calls pool callbacks, and can dispose a caller-owned object a second time after the caller's own error path already did.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/UHttpRequestBody.cs:386`

## Problem
OwnedMemoryRequestBody and StreamRequestBody declare finalizers that call DisposeCoreFromFinalizer (UHttpRequestBody.cs:386-389, :463-466), which runs DisposeCore: _owner.Dispose() on the caller's IMemoryOwner<byte> (:381-384) or _stream.Dispose() on the caller's Stream (:457-461). Both are public entry points (UHttpRequest.WithLeasedBody, WithStreamBody). architecture.md states 'A finalizer never calls pool callbacks'; UHttpResponse deliberately limits its finalizer to ArrayPool returns and skips managed callbacks (UHttpResponse.cs:308-325).

**Failure scenario.** A request built with WithLeasedBody(owner, n) is dropped after an exception before send, and the caller disposes owner in its own error path; later the finalizer disposes it again on the finalizer thread. With an owner that is not idempotent or not thread-safe (custom pool, native-backed memory) the buffer is returned twice or freed off-thread.

## Suggested fix
Remove the finalizers (a body holds only managed references) and report an undisposed body in development builds the way UHttpStreamingResponse does.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] OwnedMemoryRequestBody and StreamRequestBody have no finalizers; the caller's owner or stream is disposed only by explicit Dispose
- [ ] An undisposed body is reported in development builds, as UHttpStreamingResponse does
- [ ] Tests/Runtime/Core/: a deterministic NUnit regression test with a counting IMemoryOwner and Stream shows no dispose call after the body is dropped and collected, and fails before the fix

## Summary
StreamRequestBody and FactoryRequestBody comments say Expect: 100-continue is not implemented, although WithExpectContinue, StreamingOptions.ExpectContinueTimeoutMs and ExpectContinueHelper exist. title: [Core] UHttpResponse public constructor exposes bodyFromPool, which returns a caller array to the internal ArrayPool
body:
## Summary
The public UHttpResponse constructor accepts bodyFromPool; when true, Dispose and the finalizer return the caller's array to ArrayPool<byte>.Shared via ByteArrayPool. No runtime or test caller passes true. A test double using it with a non-bucket-sized array gets ArgumentException on Dispose or the finalizer, and a bucket-sized foreign array pollutes the shared pool and drives ByteArrayPool.ActiveCount negative.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/UHttpResponse.cs:91`

## Problem
The public constructor takes bool bodyFromPool (UHttpResponse.cs:84-92); when true, Dispose and the finalizer call ByteArrayPool.Return on the array behind the caller's memory (:104-115, :298-299, :280-283). rg finds no call site in Runtime/ or Tests/ passing true. ByteArrayPool forwards to ArrayPool<byte>.Shared.Return and increments the leak-oracle counters (Internal/ByteArrayPool.cs:91-101); the shared pool throws ArgumentException for an array whose length is not a pool bucket size.

**Failure scenario.** A test double builds new UHttpResponse(..., new byte[1000], ..., bodyFromPool: true): Dispose throws ArgumentException, or the finalizer does on the finalizer thread; with a bucket-sized array that was not rented, a foreign array enters the shared pool and ByteArrayPool.ActiveCount goes negative.

## Suggested fix
Remove the parameter from the public constructor (keep an internal overload if a friend assembly needs it).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] bodyFromPool is removed from the public constructor; an internal overload remains only if a friend assembly needs it
- [ ] Public construction with a caller array never returns that array to a pool

title: [Core] UHttpResponse.GetBodyAsString copies any body above 16 KB into a full-size temporary byte[]
body:
## Summary
Buffered bodies are held in 16 KB pooled segments, so any larger body is multi-segment and both GetBodyAsString overloads call body.ToArray(). A 2 MB response holds the segments, a 2 MB throwaway array and a 4 MB string at once, putting repeated large short-lived allocations on the mobile heap.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/UHttpResponse.cs:162`

## Problem
Buffered bodies are collected into 16 KB pooled segments (SegmentedBuffer.DefaultSegmentSize, ResponseCollectorHandler.cs:169/176), so any body above 16 KB is multi-segment and both GetBodyAsString overloads take body.ToArray() (162-163, 181-182): a temporary array of the full body size next to the pooled segments and the resulting string. Callers include OAuthClient.cs:143/189/200/240, CoroutineWrapper.cs:314 and the samples.

**Failure scenario.** A 2 MB JSON response read with GetBodyAsString holds 2 MB of pooled segments, a 2 MB throwaway byte[] and a 4 MB string at once; repeated calls put a large short-lived allocation on the non-compacting mobile heap each time.

## Suggested fix
Decode segment by segment with a Decoder into a pooled char buffer, or flatten into a ByteArrayPool rental that is returned right after GetString.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] GetBodyAsString decodes segment by segment with a Decoder, or flattens into a pooled rental returned right after decoding, with no full-size managed byte[] allocation
- [ ] Measurable target: for a multi-segment body, allocations other than the result string are bounded by a constant, not the body size
- [ ] Tests/Runtime/Core/: a deterministic NUnit regression test decodes a multi-segment body (including a multi-byte character split across a segment boundary) correctly and asserts the allocation target, failing before the fix

## Context

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Code is as described. Both overloads take body.ToArray() for a multi-segment body (Runtime/Core/UHttpResponse.cs:162-163, 181-182). The non-detached collector path writes into a SegmentedBuffer with the default 16 KB segment (Runtime/Core/Pipeline/ResponseCollectorHandler.cs:169-187, Runtime/Core/Internal/SegmentedBuffer.cs:34,42), so a body above 16 KB is multi-segment there; a detached body keeps whatever segmentation the source had. No guard or pooled path exists. Downgraded to low: this is a convenience API whose dominant cost is the string itself (2 bytes per char), the extra array is one short-lived allocation per call, not per frame, and the first-party callers are OAuth token responses (small) and CoroutineWrapper.cs:314. #120 and #434 do not cover it.

title: [Core] UHttpResponse.GetContentEncoding finds charset by substring search instead of parsing Content-Type parameters
body:
## Summary
The method takes the first occurrence of 'charset' anywhere in the Content-Type value, then the next '=', without checking that it is a parameter name after ';' or skipping quoted strings. Values such as boundary="x;charset=utf-16" or a profile URL containing charset= yield the wrong encoding and the body is decoded incorrectly.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/UHttpResponse.cs:195`

## Problem
The method takes the first occurrence of "charset" anywhere in the header value (UHttpResponse.cs:195), then the next '=' after it (199), without checking that it is a parameter name after ';' and without skipping quoted strings. Tests cover only the plain cases (Tests/Runtime/Core/JsonExtensionsTests.cs:138-180). The result is passed to Encoding.GetEncoding with a peer-chosen name (223).

**Failure scenario.** Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary="x;charset=utf-16"; charset=utf-8, or application/json; profile="https://example/charset=utf-16": the method returns UTF-16 taken from inside another parameter's quoted value and the caller decodes the body with the wrong encoding. A parameter named x-charset is matched as well.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 Sections 8.3.1 and 8.3.2

## Suggested fix
Parse the media type parameters properly: split on ';' outside quoted strings, compare the parameter name to "charset" case-insensitively, and unquote the value.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Content-Type parameters are parsed by splitting on ';' outside quoted strings; the parameter name is compared to 'charset' case-insensitively and the value is unquoted
- [ ] A parameter such as x-charset or a charset inside another parameter's quoted value is ignored

title: [Core] GetContentEncoding silently falls back to UTF-8 for code pages missing in Unity players
body:
## Summary
GetContentEncoding resolves the charset with Encoding.GetEncoding and maps every failure to UTF-8 in a bare catch. Unity players carry only the built-in encodings unless I18N assemblies are linked, so windows-1252, shift_jis, gb2312 or euc-kr resolve in the Editor but decode as UTF-8 with replacement characters on iOS and Android. No diagnostic is written and the exception recurs on every call.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/UHttpResponse.cs:223`

## Problem
GetContentEncoding (189-229) resolves the charset with Encoding.GetEncoding(name) and maps every failure to UTF-8 in a bare catch (221-228). Unity players (Mono and IL2CPP) carry only the built-in encodings (UTF-8/16/32, ASCII, Latin-1); the I18N code-page assemblies are not linked unless the project adds them, so windows-1252, shift_jis, gb2312 or euc-kr throw there but resolve in the Editor. No diagnostic is written and the exception is thrown again on each call.

**Failure scenario.** A response with Content-Type: text/html; charset=windows-1252 (or shift_jis): GetBodyAsString(response.GetContentEncoding()) decodes correctly in the Editor and as UTF-8 with replacement characters on an iOS or Android player.

## Suggested fix
Resolve the Latin-1 family without Encoding.GetEncoding, cache the resolved charset per response, and report an unsupported charset once through TurboDiagnostics.LogOnce (or expose a Try variant) so a fallback can be told from a match. Confirm the available code pages in an IL2CPP player.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The Latin-1 family is resolved without Encoding.GetEncoding
- [ ] The resolved charset is cached per response and an unsupported charset is reported once through TurboDiagnostics.LogOnce, or a Try variant lets callers tell fallback from match
- [ ] Available code pages are confirmed in an IL2CPP player and validated on a device and recorded
- [ ] Tests/Runtime/Core/: a deterministic NUnit regression test with an unsupported charset asserts the single diagnostic and no repeated exception, failing before the fix

title: [Core] UHttpResponse finalizer returns pooled body buffers to ArrayPool while a copied-out Body sequence may still reference them
body:
## Summary
The finalizer calls Dispose(false), which returns the pooled body buffer and disposes the segmented body owner, returning segments to ArrayPool.Shared. Body hands out a ReadOnlySequence<byte> that references those arrays but not the response, so code that keeps only the sequence can see the response finalized and the buffers reused by another request's collector, reading another request's bytes silently.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/UHttpResponse.cs:280`

## Problem
~UHttpResponse (280-283) calls Dispose(false), which returns _pooledBodyBuffer through ByteArrayPool.Return (298-299) and disposes _segmentedBodyOwner (304-305): SegmentedBuffer.Dispose -> PooledSegment.ReturnToPool -> ArrayPool.Shared.Return (SegmentedBuffer.cs:186-228, PooledSegment.cs:86-92), or the HTTP/2 ArrayPoolMemoryOwner (Http2ResponseBodySource.cs:161-164). Body (37-44) hands out a ReadOnlySequence<byte> struct that references those arrays but not the response; GetBodyAsString (153-164) and JsonExtensions.cs:33 keep reading the sequence after their last use of the response object and nothing calls GC.KeepAlive. architecture.md ("Ownership transfer") forbids returning a buffer another thread may still touch.

**Failure scenario.** Code keeps the sequence, a segment or a Memory slice but not the response (var body = (await req.SendBufferedAsync()).Body;): the GC finalizes the response, its 16 KB segments go back to ArrayPool.Shared, the next response collector rents them, and the caller reads another request's bytes (silent corruption and cross-request data exposure). Without the finalizer return the same mistake would only cost garbage. Under a precise GC the window also exists inside (await ...).GetBodyAsString() / AsJson<T>() on a temporary response.

## Suggested fix
On the finalizer path do not return buffers to the pool: leave them to the GC and account them with ByteArrayPool.Abandon so the #292 leak counter stays exact; keep pool returns for explicit Dispose. Add GC.KeepAlive(this) at the end of the GetBodyAsString overloads.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The finalizer path does not return buffers to the pool; they are left to the GC and accounted with ByteArrayPool.Abandon so the leak counter stays exact
- [ ] Pool returns remain only on explicit Dispose
- [ ] GC.KeepAlive(this) is added at the end of the GetBodyAsString overloads
- [ ] Tests/Runtime/Core/: a deterministic NUnit regression test keeps only the Body sequence, forces finalization, then rents buffers and asserts the sequence content is unchanged, failing before the fix

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `core-runtime-03` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/core.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: resource-management.

Verification: Plausible: the code is as described; the outcome depends on runtime, device or peer behaviour that a static review cannot settle.

Verifier note: Code is as described: ~UHttpResponse (UHttpResponse.cs:280-283) runs Dispose(false), which returns _pooledBodyBuffer through ByteArrayPool.Return (298-299) and disposes _segmentedBodyOwner (304-305), i.e. hands the body arrays back to ArrayPool. Body (37-44) returns a ReadOnlySequence<byte> struct that references the arrays but not the response, and GetBodyAsString (153-164) has no GC.KeepAlive(this). So code that keeps the sequence or a slice while the response becomes unreachable can read arrays re-rented by another request. The XML remarks (29-36) forbid use after Dispose, but dropping the response is the same mistake made silently, and the finalizer turns it from garbage into cross-request corruption for no real gain (unreturned ArrayPool arrays are just collected). Plausible rather than confirmed: it needs caller misuse plus GC and finalizer timing; the in-method window on a temporary response is narrow under Boehm's conservative stack scan on Mono/IL2CPP and cannot be settled statically. architecture.md:111 ('A finalizer never calls pool callbacks') is about callbacks; the comments at 296-303 argue thread safety of the return, not aliasing, so the documented trade-off does not cover this.

title: [Core] Dropped UHttpStreamingResponse never aborts its body source, leaking the HTTP/1.1 lease and per-host permit; release builds keep an empty finalizer
body:
## Summary
The UHttpStreamingResponse finalizer only counts and logs under debug builds, is empty in release builds yet still registers every instance for finalization, and never calls Abort on the body source. The source owns the ConnectionLease, released only on complete or close. Dropping a response with an unread body leaks the connection lease and host permit for the life of the transport.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/UHttpStreamingResponse.cs:77`

## Problem
The finalizer (77-87) only counts and logs under DEBUG || UNITY_EDITOR || DEVELOPMENT_BUILD; in release builds its body is empty, yet the type still has a finalizer, so every streaming response is registered for finalization for no effect. It never calls _bodySource.Abort(). The source is the only owner of the transport resources: Http11ResponseBodySource keeps the ConnectionLease (Http11ResponseBodySource.cs:59) and releases it only in CompleteBody/CloseBody (660-684); ConnectionLease (TcpConnectionPool.cs:152) releases the per-host SemaphoreSlim permit only from Dispose/ReturnToPool/TransferOwnership; neither type has a finalizer (the only finalizers in Runtime outside vendored code are the four in Core). The attached release callbacks (request hold, RequestContext.CompleteAfterResponse) are never run either.

**Failure scenario.** Application code drops a streaming response with an unread body (an exception between SendStreamingAsync and the using, or a forgotten dispose) MaxConnectionsPerHost times for one host over HTTP/1.1 (8 on mobile): every permit of that host is gone, later requests to it wait for a permit until their timeout, and a release build logs nothing.

## Suggested fix
Give the dropped response a backstop in every build: from the finalizer queue a static thread-pool callback that calls Abort() on the body source (no managed callbacks on the finalizer thread), or make the lease itself finalizer-safe. If the finalizer stays diagnostics-only, compile the whole finalizer out of release builds.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A dropped streaming response releases its lease and permit in every build, by queuing a static thread-pool callback that calls Abort on the body source (no managed callbacks on the finalizer thread) or by making the lease finalizer-safe
- [ ] If the finalizer stays diagnostics-only, the whole finalizer is compiled out of release builds
- [ ] After MaxConnectionsPerHost dropped responses to one host, a further request to that host still acquires a permit

title: [Core] Synchronous Dispose of UHttpStreamingResponse aborts the body instead of draining, losing the keep-alive connection
body:
## Summary
StartBodyDispose calls Abort whenever end of stream was not observed, whereas DisposeAsync lets the HTTP/1.1 body source drain up to its threshold and return the connection to the pool. Abort closes the lease. A caller that disposes synchronously after reading a small 404 body or a chunked body short of the final read closes the connection, and the next request pays a new TCP and TLS handshake.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/UHttpStreamingResponse.cs:157`

## Problem
StartBodyDispose (155-161) calls _bodySource.Abort() whenever the stream has not observed end of stream; only DisposeAsync (227-237) lets the source decide. Http11ResponseBodySource.DisposeAsync drains up to BufferedDrainReuseThresholdBytes and returns the connection to the pool (279-311, 450-468), whereas Abort -> CloseBody disposes the lease (254-258, 675-684). The non-blocking continuation a pending drain needs already exists (CompleteDisposeWhenBodyDisposed, 189-218).

**Failure scenario.** using var response = await request.SendStreamingAsync(); the caller returns after seeing a 404 with a 300-byte body, or after reading a chunked body up to but not including the final zero-length read: Dispose closes the HTTP/1.1 connection and the next request to that host pays a new TCP and TLS handshake, where await using would have reused it.

## Suggested fix
In Dispose always start _bodySource.DisposeAsync() and hand an incomplete task to CompleteDisposeWhenBodyDisposed; keep Abort for the failure path.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Synchronous Dispose always starts _bodySource.DisposeAsync() and hands an incomplete task to CompleteDisposeWhenBodyDisposed; Abort is kept for the failure path
- [ ] After a sync Dispose with a small remaining body, the HTTP/1.1 connection returns to the pool and is reused by the next request to the host
- [ ] Tests/Runtime/Core/: a deterministic NUnit regression test counts connections opened across two requests with a sync Dispose between them, failing before the fix
